topics.title: High blood pressure
short: The force of blood on your blood vessel walls stays too high.
Most people feel nothing, so only a check can tell.
Over the years it can harm the heart, brain and kidneys.
goNow: Sudden weakness or numbness of the face, arm or leg, or trouble speaking
Crushing chest pain or pain that spreads to the arm or jaw
A very bad headache with confusion, or trouble seeing
A reading of 180/120 or higher with chest pain, short breath, a bad headache, or trouble seeing or speaking: call 911

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Blood pressure is the push of blood against the walls of your blood vessels. When the top number stays at 140 or higher, or the bottom number at 90 or higher, it is called high blood pressure. Your doctor will say what number is right for you.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Often none at all
Headache, dizziness or a pounding in the chest can happen, but not always
A check at the health centre or at home is the only sure way

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take your medicine every day, even when you feel well
Eat less salt, patis, toyo and instant noodles
Walk most days if your doctor says it is safe
Do not smoke, and limit alcohol

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Check your pressure at least once a year, more often if you are over 40
Keep a healthy weight
Eat more vegetables and fruit
Move your body every day

videos.source: Gabay sa Kalusugan - Dr. Gary Sy

videos.title: 14 tips to control high blood pressure (in Filipino)

topics.title: Heart attack
short: A heart attack happens when blood cannot reach part of the heart.
It is an emergency, and every minute counts.
Fast treatment can save the heart and save a life.
goNow: Chest pain or pressure that lasts more than a few minutes
Pain in the arm, back, neck or jaw, with sweating or feeling sick
Trouble breathing, or feeling faint with chest discomfort
Call 911 or go to the nearest hospital now. Do not drive yourself.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A heart attack happens when a blocked blood vessel stops blood from reaching part of the heart. The heart muscle starts to be damaged. Women, older people and people with diabetes may have fewer clear signs.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Pressure, squeezing or heavy feeling in the chest
Pain that moves to the arm, back, neck or jaw
Cold sweat, feeling sick, short of breath
In women and older people: unusual tiredness or tummy discomfort

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
While you wait for help, sit down and stay calm
Loosen tight clothes
If a doctor has told you to take aspirin for this, follow that advice
Never wait to see if it passes
If the person collapses and is not breathing normally, start hands-only CPR

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol in check
Do not smoke
Eat less salty and fatty food
Stay active and keep a healthy weight

videos.title: Warning signs of a heart attack (in Filipino)

topics.title: Stroke
short: A stroke is a sudden loss of blood flow to part of the brain.
Learn BE FAST: Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech, Time.
Getting to a hospital in the first hours can save a life.
goNow: One side of the face droops when the person smiles
One arm is weak or numb, or cannot be lifted
Speech is slurred or strange, or the person cannot understand you
Sudden loss of balance or vision, or a very bad headache. Call 911 now and note the time it began.
Go now even if the signs go away after a few minutes.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A stroke happens when a blood vessel in the brain is blocked or bursts. Brain cells start to die within minutes. Quick treatment can save brain and life. High blood pressure is the biggest cause.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Face drooping on one side
Arm or leg weakness on one side
Slurred speech or confusion
Sudden trouble seeing or walking
Sudden very bad headache

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Do not give food, drink or medicine by mouth
Lay the person down with the head a little raised
Note the time the signs began and tell the hospital
After a stroke, follow your rehab plan and take medicines as told
Do not prick the fingers or ears, or give any medicine

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep blood pressure under control
Do not smoke
Stay active
Eat less salt and less fatty food
Take heart medicines as prescribed

videos.title: Stroke: 8 Warning Signs
BE FAST: signs of a stroke

topics.title: Angina (chest pain from the heart)
short: Angina is chest pain when the heart does not get enough blood.
It often comes with effort and eases with rest.
It is a warning sign. See a doctor soon.
goNow: Chest pain that lasts more than 5 minutes, or does not ease with rest or your heart medicine: call 911 now. Do not drive yourself.
Pain with sweating, feeling faint, or trouble breathing
Pain that is new, worse, or comes at rest

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Angina is a pressure or squeezing pain in the chest. It happens when the heart muscle does not get enough blood, often because vessels are narrowed. It is not a heart attack, but it can be a warning of one.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Pressure or tightness in the chest
Pain that spreads to the shoulder, arm, neck or jaw
Short of breath or tired with effort
Pain that eases after rest

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Stop and rest when pain comes
Take the medicine your doctor gave you for it
Avoid heavy meals and strong effort in the heat
Keep your follow-up visits

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not smoke
Control blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol
Keep active in a way your doctor allows
Keep a healthy weight

topics.title: Heart failure
short: The heart is weak and cannot pump blood as well as it should.
It does not mean the heart has stopped.
Medicines, less salt and daily checks keep people well.
goNow: Sudden bad shortness of breath, or you cannot lie flat
Chest pain, fainting, or a very fast heartbeat
Coughing up pink, foamy spit

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In heart failure the heart muscle is too weak or stiff to pump enough blood for the body. Fluid can then build up in the lungs, legs and tummy. It is a long-term illness that can be managed well.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Short of breath, especially lying down
Swollen feet, ankles or tummy
Tiredness and weakness
Quick weight gain over a few days
Cough at night

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take medicines every day
Weigh yourself each morning and tell your doctor about a quick gain
Eat less salt
Ask your doctor how much to drink
Keep your follow-up visits

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep blood pressure and sugar under control
Do not smoke
Treat heart disease early
Limit alcohol

topics.title: High cholesterol
short: Too much cholesterol in the blood can block blood vessels over time.
You cannot feel it. A blood test shows it.
Food, activity and sometimes medicine bring it down.
goNow: Chest pain or pressure, or signs of a stroke, are an emergency. Call 911.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Cholesterol is a fatty substance in your blood. Some is needed, but too much LDL ("bad") cholesterol can build up in your blood vessels. This raises the chance of heart attack and stroke. Family history can also play a part.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Usually none
Found by a blood test called a lipid profile

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Eat less fried food, fatty meat, chicharon and coconut cream foods
Eat more fish, vegetables, oats and beans
Take your medicine as told
Walk or move 30 minutes on most days

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Get tested from age 40, or earlier if heart disease runs in your family
Keep a healthy weight
Do not smoke
Limit sweet drinks and alcohol

videos.title: Cholesterol numbers

topics.title: Irregular heartbeat
short: The heart beats too fast, too slow, or in an uneven way.
Many cases are harmless, but some raise the risk of stroke.
A doctor can check it with a heart tracing (ECG).
goNow: Fainting, or chest pain with a fast heartbeat
A fast heartbeat with trouble breathing
Signs of a stroke: face droop, weak arm, slurred speech

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: An irregular heartbeat is called an arrhythmia. Atrial fibrillation is a common type where the top of the heart quivers. It can cause blood clots, so it raises stroke risk. Some people need medicines to thin the blood.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
A fluttering or racing heart
Dizziness or feeling faint
Short of breath
Tiredness
Some people feel nothing

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take heart and blood-thinning medicines exactly as told
Cut down coffee, energy drinks, alcohol and cigarettes
Tell your doctor about all your medicines
Keep your check-ups

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Control blood pressure
Keep a healthy weight
Limit alcohol
Ask about sleep apnea if you snore loudly

topics.title: Heart disease (blocked heart vessels)
short: Fatty build-up narrows the vessels that feed the heart.
It is the most common heart disease.
It can lead to chest pain or a heart attack.
goNow: Chest pain that does not ease with rest within a few minutes
Pain with sweating, nausea or trouble breathing
Call 911 or go to the hospital now

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Fatty deposits called plaque slowly narrow the blood vessels of the heart. Less blood reaches the heart muscle. Over many years this can cause chest pain, a heart attack or heart failure.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Chest pain or pressure with effort
Short of breath
Unusual tiredness
Some people have no signs until a heart attack

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take aspirin, statin and blood pressure medicines only as your doctor says
Eat less salt and fat
Stay active in a way your doctor allows
Keep your appointments

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not smoke
Control blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol
Keep a healthy weight
Move every day

topics.title: Cardiac arrest and CPR
short: In cardiac arrest the heart stops and the person collapses.
Hands-only CPR can keep blood moving until help arrives.
Anyone can do it. You cannot make it worse.
goNow: A person who suddenly collapses, will not wake and is not breathing normally: call 911 now

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: When the heart stops, blood stops reaching the brain. Hands-only CPR means pushing hard and fast on the centre of the chest, about twice a second. Do this until help or an AED arrives, or the person wakes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Collapse without warning
Will not wake when you shout and shake the shoulders
Not breathing, or only gasping

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Call 911 or ask someone to call
Send someone to find an AED (a shock machine) if there is one
Place the heel of one hand on the centre of the chest, the other hand on top
Push down hard, about 5 cm for an adult, and let the chest come back up
Start pushing hard and fast on the centre of the chest
Start pushing hard and fast on the centre of the chest
Keep going without stopping until help takes over

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Learn CPR from the Red Cross
Treat heart disease early
Know where the nearest AED is in your building

videos.title: Hands-only CPR
Be prepared for emergencies with hands-only CPR

topics.title: Low blood pressure and dizziness
short: Low blood pressure can make you dizzy or faint.
It is only a problem when it causes signs.
Standing up slowly and drinking enough water often help.
goNow: Fainting with chest pain, or a very fast heartbeat
Confusion, cold clammy skin, or very fast breathing
Fainting after a head injury, or black or bloody stools

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Blood pressure that is lower than normal is called low blood pressure. For some people it is normal. It becomes a problem when you feel dizzy or faint. Causes include dehydration, some medicines, bleeding and heart problems.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Dizziness when you stand up
Blurred vision
Feeling faint or weak
Cold, pale skin

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Sit or lie down at once when dizzy
Drink water or oral rehydration salts
Stand up slowly from bed
Tell your doctor which medicines you take

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink enough fluids, especially in the heat
Do not stand still for a long time in hot places
Review blood pressure medicines with your doctor

topics.title: Blood clot in the leg
short: A blood clot can form in a deep vein, often in the leg.
The clot can travel to the lungs and be life-threatening.
Long sitting, bed rest and surgery raise the risk.
goNow: Sudden short breath or chest pain, especially with a swollen leg
Coughing up blood
A very swollen, red, painful leg that is warm to touch

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a blood clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg. If a piece breaks off and reaches the lungs, it can block blood flow. This is called a pulmonary embolism and needs emergency care.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
One leg swollen, painful or warm
Skin red or dark
Pain in the calf, like a cramp
Sudden breathlessness is an emergency

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take blood-thinning medicine exactly as prescribed
Tell your doctor before any surgery or new medicine
Walk as your doctor allows

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Move and stretch your legs on long trips
Walk soon after surgery or illness if allowed
Drink enough water
Do not smoke

topics.title: Poor blood flow in the legs
short: Narrow blood vessels can starve the legs of blood.
Leg pain when walking that eases with rest is a clue.
It often goes with diabetes and smoking.
goNow: A leg that suddenly turns cold, pale or blue and very painful
A sore on the foot that will not heal, or black skin
Fever with a red, swollen foot

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In peripheral arterial disease, fatty build-up narrows the vessels that carry blood to the legs. Muscles do not get enough blood when you walk. Wounds on the feet heal slowly, which is serious in people with diabetes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Cramping leg or calf pain when walking
Cold feet or toes
Sores that heal slowly
Shiny skin or less hair on the legs

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Check your feet every day
Wear soft shoes and clean socks
Walk a little, rest, then walk again as your doctor advises
Take medicines as told

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Stop smoking
Control sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol
Keep active
Take care of your feet

topics.title: Rheumatic heart disease
aka: sore throat that harms the heart
short: A sore throat from strep germs, left untreated, can harm the heart valves.
It mostly affects children and young people.
Treating a sore throat early prevents it.
goNow: Chest pain, short breath or swollen ankles in someone who had rheumatic fever
A child with fever, painful swollen joints and a new rash after a sore throat

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Rheumatic fever can follow a strep throat that was not fully treated. The body's reaction can scar the heart valves. This is rheumatic heart disease. It can cause heart failure later in life. It is still common where strep throat goes untreated.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever and sore throat that comes back
Painful, swollen joints
Short of breath or tiredness
A rash on the chest or back

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Finish all antibiotics a doctor prescribes for a sore throat
Keep regular check-ups if you have a heart valve problem
Ask your doctor about monthly penicillin if advised

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
See a doctor for a sore throat with fever
Finish the full course of antibiotics
Wash hands often

topics.title: Aneurysm
short: An aneurysm is a weak bulge in a blood vessel wall.
Most are silent until they burst.
A burst is an emergency.
goNow: Sudden, severe tearing pain in the chest, back or tummy
Sudden worst headache of your life, or stiff neck with vomiting
Fainting or a rapid heartbeat with severe pain

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: An aneurysm is a bulge in the wall of a blood vessel. It can form in the brain or in the large vessel of the chest or tummy. If it bursts, bleeding can be life-threatening. High blood pressure and smoking raise the risk.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Often none
Pulsing feeling in the tummy
Sudden severe headache or back pain when it leaks or bursts

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep blood pressure under control
Take medicines as told
Keep follow-up scans

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not smoke
Control blood pressure
Eat less salt
Tell your doctor if close family had an aneurysm

topics.title: Asthma
short: Asthma makes the breathing tubes swell and narrow.
It comes in attacks of wheeze, cough and tight chest.
A reliever inhaler and a plan from your doctor keep it safe.
goNow: Lips or face turn blue or grey
Cannot speak a full sentence, or struggles for each breath
The reliever inhaler does not help, or helps for less than a few hours
Call 911 or go to the hospital now

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Asthma is a long-term illness of the breathing tubes. They become swollen and tight, and make extra mucus. Dust, smoke, cold air, colds, pets and strong smells can start an attack. It can be well controlled.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Wheezing, a whistle when breathing out
Cough, worse at night or early morning
Tight chest
Short of breath

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Sit upright, stay calm and use your reliever inhaler as your doctor taught you
Take your daily controller medicine even when well
Stay away from smoke, dust and mold
Keep a written asthma plan

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Learn and avoid your triggers
Do not smoke and avoid smoky rooms
Wash bedding often
Get a flu shot every year

topics.title: COPD (long-term lung disease)
short: COPD slowly makes it harder to breathe out.
Smoking is the main cause.
Stopping smoking and using inhalers slows it down.
goNow: Breathing is much harder than usual, or you cannot speak in full sentences
Blue lips or fingers, or new confusion or drowsiness
Chest pain, or coughing up blood

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: COPD is a long-term lung illness that includes chronic bronchitis and emphysema. The air tubes are damaged and narrowed, so air gets out slowly. It does not go away, but treatment and no smoking help you feel better and slow it down.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Cough that lasts for months, often with phlegm
Short of breath with walking or stairs
Wheezing
Tight chest
Many chest infections

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Stop smoking and stay away from smoke and cooking smoke
Use inhalers as prescribed
Get flu and pneumonia shots
Ask about breathing exercises and rehab

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not start smoking, or quit
Use a chimney or open a window when cooking with wood
Wear a mask in dust
Treat chest infections early

topics.title: Pneumonia
short: Pneumonia is an infection that fills the lungs with fluid.
It can be mild, or it can be life-threatening.
Babies, older people and sick people need care fast.
goNow: Fast, hard or painful breathing, or chest pulling in with each breath
Blue lips, or a child too sleepy to feed or drink
Confusion in an older person, or a high fever with shaking
Coughing up blood

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs caused by germs such as bacteria and viruses. The tiny air sacs fill with fluid and it becomes hard to breathe. It can come after a cold or flu. Antibiotics help only when the cause is bacteria, so a doctor must decide.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Cough with phlegm
Fever and chills
Fast breathing and short of breath
Chest pain when breathing or coughing
Feeling very tired

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor, do not treat it alone
Take the full course of any medicine prescribed
Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Do not smoke

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Get the flu and pneumonia vaccines
Wash hands often
Do not smoke
Keep children's vaccines up to date

videos.title: Pneumonia: Simple Health Remedies

topics.title: Tuberculosis (TB)
short: TB is a germ that spreads in the air and mostly harms the lungs.
Free tests and treatment are given at health centres.
It can usually be cured if you take all the medicine, usually for six months or more.
goNow: Coughing up blood
Chest pain, or very hard breathing
High fever with severe weakness, or a child who is very sick

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: TB is an infection caused by a germ. It spreads when a person with TB in the lungs coughs or sneezes. Not everyone who is infected gets sick. TB is curable with medicines taken every day for months. Stopping early can make it come back stronger.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
A cough that lasts more than two weeks
Coughing up blood
Night sweats and fever
Weight loss and no appetite
Tiredness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take all medicine every day for the whole time, even when you feel well
Cover your mouth when you cough and open windows
Go to the health centre for free TB tests and care (DOTS)
Eat well

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Test people living with someone who has TB
Open windows to let in fresh air
Complete the full treatment so it cannot spread
Have newborns vaccinated with BCG

videos.title: Tuberculosis (TB): signs and treatment (in Filipino)

topics.title: Bronchitis
short: Bronchitis is swelling of the tubes that carry air to the lungs.
Most cases come from a virus and get better on their own.
A cough can last two or three weeks.
goNow: Trouble breathing, or fast breathing
Coughing up blood, or a fever above 38.5 C that stays
A cough that lasts longer than three weeks

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In bronchitis the tubes that carry air in your lungs are swollen and make mucus. It often follows a cold or flu and is caused by a virus. Antibiotics do not help a virus. Rest and fluids are usually enough.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Cough with clear, white or yellow phlegm
Sore chest
Tired
Mild fever and chills
Wheeze

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest and drink plenty of water
Warm drinks such as warm water with honey soothe the cough (not for babies under 1 year)
Stay away from smoke
Use a clean cloth or mask when you cough

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not smoke
Wash hands often
Get the flu vaccine
Stay away from people with colds when you can

topics.title: Cough
short: Cough clears the airway and is often from a cold.
A cough over two weeks should be checked for TB and other causes.
Children, older people and smokers need extra care.
goNow: Trouble breathing or fast breathing
Coughing up blood
Cough with chest pain, a high fever, or blue lips
Choking, or a cough after eating or drinking

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A cough is the way your body clears the throat and airways. Most coughs come from a cold, flu or allergy and go away in a week or two. A cough that lasts longer needs a check. In the Philippines, a cough over two weeks should be checked for TB.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Dry cough or cough with phlegm
Sore throat
Blocked nose
Cough at night from reflux, asthma or allergy

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Drink warm fluids
Warm water with honey can soothe the cough (not for babies under 1 year)
Do not give cough syrups to young children unless a doctor says
Keep away from smoke and dust

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wash hands
Do not smoke
Cover your cough
Keep rooms clean and dust-free

topics.title: Flu (influenza)
short: The flu is a virus that spreads easily, most often in the rainy season.
It brings fever, body aches, cough and tiredness.
A yearly flu shot lowers the risk, mostly for older people and children.
goNow: Trouble breathing or chest pain
Confusion, or very hard to wake up
Fever that goes away then comes back worse, or lasts more than 3 days in a child
A baby with fever, or someone who cannot drink

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Influenza is a virus that infects the nose, throat and lungs. It spreads by cough, sneeze and touch. Most people get better in about a week. It can turn serious in babies, older people, pregnant women and people with heart, lung or kidney illness.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Sudden fever and chills
Body aches and headache
Dry cough
Sore throat, runny nose
Tiredness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest and drink plenty of water
Paracetamol may ease fever and aches (follow the pack, no aspirin for children)
Stay home so others do not catch it
Wear a mask around other people

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Get a flu shot every year
Wash hands often
Cover your cough
Stay home when sick

topics.title: Common cold
short: A cold is a mild virus infection of the nose and throat.
It gets better by itself in about a week.
Antibiotics do not help a cold.
goNow: Trouble breathing
A baby under 3 months with any fever
Fever over 3 days, or signs that get worse after a week

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Many viruses cause the common cold. It spreads by hands, coughs and sneezes. Antibiotics do not work against viruses. Most people feel better in 7 to 10 days.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Runny or blocked nose
Sneezing
Sore throat
Mild cough
Mild tiredness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest and drink plenty of water
Warm drinks soothe the throat
Salt water gargle for sore throat
Wash hands and use tissue or your elbow when you sneeze

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wash your hands often
Do not share cups
Keep away from sick people
Sleep well

topics.title: COVID-19
short: COVID-19 is caused by a virus that spreads through the air.
Many people have mild illness, but some become very sick.
Vaccines lower the chance of serious illness.
goNow: Trouble breathing, or fast breathing
Chest pain or pressure that does not go away
New confusion, blue lips, or unable to wake up

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. It spreads when people breathe, cough or speak near each other. Older people and people with heart, lung, kidney or sugar problems are at higher risk of serious illness.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever or chills
Cough
Sore throat
Loss of smell or taste
Body aches and tiredness
Short of breath

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Stay home and wear a mask around others
Paracetamol may ease fever
Call your doctor early if you are at higher risk

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Stay up to date with vaccines
Wear a mask in crowded or closed places
Wash hands
Open windows for fresh air

topics.title: Sinus infection
short: Sinusitis is swelling in the air spaces behind the nose and cheeks.
It often follows a cold.
Most cases get better without antibiotics.
goNow: Swelling or redness around the eye, or changes in eyesight
A bad headache with stiff neck or confusion
A high fever that does not go away

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The sinuses are small air spaces in the face. When they swell and fill with mucus, the face feels full and painful. A cold is the usual cause. Many cases go away in 10 days without antibiotics.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Blocked or runny nose
Pain or pressure in the cheeks, forehead or around the eyes
Headache
Cough, bad breath
Feeling tired

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest and drink water
Breathe steam from a warm bowl, with care not to burn yourself
Use salt-water nasal rinse that is clean
See a doctor if it lasts more than 10 days

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Treat colds and allergies early
Do not smoke
Wash hands

topics.title: Hay fever (allergic rhinitis)
short: An allergy to dust, pollen or pets can cause a runny, itchy nose.
It is not a cold and it is not catching.
Avoiding triggers and allergy medicine help.
goNow: Trouble breathing, wheeze or tight chest
Swelling of the face, lips or tongue
A rash with trouble breathing

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Allergic rhinitis happens when the body overreacts to something harmless like dust mites, pollen, mold or animal hair. The nose and eyes get itchy and runny. It is not an infection. If it comes with wheezing, it may be asthma.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Sneezing many times
Runny, itchy or blocked nose
Itchy, watery eyes
Dark circles under the eyes

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Wash bedding often in hot water
Keep pets out of bedrooms
Dust with a damp cloth
Ask a pharmacist about allergy medicine

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Find and avoid your triggers
Keep windows shut in high-pollen days
Clean air filters
Do not smoke

topics.title: Sleep apnea
short: Breathing stops for a few seconds again and again while you sleep.
Loud snoring and daytime sleepiness are clues.
It raises the risk of high blood pressure and stroke.
goNow: Falling asleep while driving or at work
Chest pain or a very fast heartbeat at night
Waking up gasping often, with a morning headache

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In sleep apnea the airway at the back of the throat closes while you sleep. You wake just enough to breathe, many times a night, and you do not feel rested. Being overweight is a common cause. A sleep test confirms it.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Loud snoring
Choking or gasping at night
Very sleepy by day
Morning headaches
Low mood or trouble focusing

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Lose weight if overweight
Sleep on your side
Avoid alcohol and sleeping pills before bed
Ask your doctor about a CPAP machine

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Do not smoke
Limit alcohol
See a doctor if you snore loudly

topics.title: Quit smoking
short: Quitting smoking helps your lungs and heart at any age.
Most people need more than one try.
Help is free through the DOH quitline and health centres.
goNow: Chest pain, short of breath or coughing blood: see a doctor now
Feeling hopeless or thinking of self-harm while quitting: get help now

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Smoking harms the lungs, heart and blood vessels and causes many cancers. Vapes also contain nicotine and are not safe. After you quit, your heart and lungs start to heal within weeks. Counselling and nicotine replacement can double your chance.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Cravings that pass in a few minutes
Feeling edgy or sad for a few weeks
Cough for a time as lungs clear
Hunger

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Choose a quit date and tell your family
Throw away all yosi and lighters
Ask a doctor or pharmacist about nicotine patches or gum
Keep busy, drink water, take a walk when a craving comes

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Never start
Avoid places with smoke
Keep children away from secondhand smoke
Ask for help when you want to quit

topics.title: Whooping cough
short: Whooping cough is a serious cough illness, most dangerous for babies.
A vaccine in the baby shots protects against it.
A baby with long coughing fits needs a doctor at once.
goNow: A baby who stops breathing, turns blue, or gasps after coughing
Vomiting after coughing, in a baby or child
Any baby under 6 months with a long cough

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Whooping cough is a bacterial infection of the airways. It causes long coughing fits that end with a "whoop" sound when the child breathes in. Babies may not whoop, but may stop breathing. Antibiotics help if given early.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Runny nose and mild cough at first
Then long, hard coughing fits
A "whoop" sound on breathing in
Vomiting after coughing
Tired after a fit

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor, mostly for babies
Keep the child away from others until treated
Small feeds more often
Keep the child upright after a fit

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Give all baby vaccines on time
Pregnant women can get a booster in late pregnancy, ask your doctor
Keep sick people away from babies

topics.title: Dengue
short: Dengue is a virus spread by day-biting mosquitoes, most often in the rainy season.
Many people recover at home, but some get very sick on days 3 to 7.
Watch for warning signs once the fever drops.
goNow: Bleeding from the nose or gums, black stools or vomit with blood
Bad tummy pain that does not stop, or vomiting again and again
Very sleepy, restless, or cold clammy skin when the fever goes down
Cannot drink, or very little urine
Go to the hospital now. Do not wait for the next day.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Dengue is a virus spread by the bite of the Aedes mosquito, which bites in the daytime. Most people recover with rest and fluids. A small number get severe dengue, which can cause bleeding and shock. The risk is highest a few days after the fever starts, often just as the fever drops.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Sudden high fever for 2 to 7 days
Bad headache and pain behind the eyes
Muscle and joint pain
Rash and mild bleeding of the nose or gums
Feeling very tired

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest and drink lots of fluids such as water, oral rehydration salts and soup
Use paracetamol for fever and follow the pack
Use paracetamol only. Do not take aspirin, ibuprofen or mefenamic acid: they raise the risk of bleeding
See a doctor for a blood test, then daily checks until the fever is gone for 2 days

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Remove standing water weekly: tires, cans, pots, gutters
Cover water drums and change vase water
Use mosquito repellent and long sleeves in the daytime
Use nets or screens for babies and bed-ridden people

videos.title: WHO Science in 5: Dengue Fever
What is dengue?

topics.title: Leptospirosis
short: A germ in rat urine gets into water, especially floodwater.
It can enter through cuts or the eyes, nose and mouth.
Early treatment with antibiotics works best.
goNow: Yellow eyes or skin, very little urine, or swollen face
Trouble breathing or coughing blood
Bad headache with stiff neck, or confusion
Bleeding or purple spots on the skin
Go to the hospital now. Say you waded in floodwater.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Leptospirosis is caused by bacteria found in the urine of rats and other animals. It spreads when floodwater or mud with those germs touches cuts or the eyes, nose or mouth. It is common after floods and typhoons. Early treatment with antibiotics prevents serious illness.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever and chills, often 2 days to 2 weeks after contact
Headache
Muscle pain, especially the calves
Red eyes
Vomiting or diarrhoea

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Do not wait to see if it passes: see a doctor within a day if you had floodwater contact and a fever
Wash your feet and legs with soap and clean water after wading
Ask about a preventive antibiotic from the health centre after a flood
Rest and drink fluids

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Avoid wading in floodwater
Wear boots and cover cuts
Keep garbage covered and control rats
Wash and dry your legs after contact

videos.title: Floods: leptospirosis and typhoid fever (in Filipino)
Lumusong sa Baha, Babala sa Leptospirosis, Typhoid Fever

topics.title: Typhoid fever
short: Typhoid comes from food or water dirtied with germs.
It brings a fever that rises day by day.
Antibiotics treat it, and a vaccine can prevent it.
goNow: Bad tummy pain with a hard belly, or black stools
Confusion, or very sleepy and weak
Fever that keeps rising with vomiting, or cannot drink

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Typhoid is a bacterial infection spread by food or water that has the germ, often after floods. It is passed by people who do not wash hands after the toilet. A doctor can test the blood to be sure. Antibiotics work, but you must finish the course.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever that goes higher each day
Headache, tiredness
Tummy pain, constipation or diarrhoea
Loss of appetite
A few pink spots on the chest

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor for tests and antibiotics
Finish the full antibiotics
Drink clean, safe water and oral rehydration salts
Do not prepare food for others until a doctor says it is safe

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink boiled or bottled water
Wash hands with soap after the toilet and before food
Eat well-cooked food
Ask about the typhoid vaccine

topics.title: Diarrhoea
short: Diarrhoea is loose, watery stools three or more times a day.
The main danger is losing too much water.
Oral rehydration salts (ORS) and clean water save lives.
goNow: Signs of dehydration: very dry mouth, no tears, sunken eyes, very little urine
Blood in the stool, or black stools
A baby under 6 months, or a child too weak to drink
High fever, or diarrhoea for more than 2 days (more than 1 day in a baby)

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Diarrhoea is often caused by a stomach infection from food or water. It usually clears in a few days. The risk is dehydration, especially in babies, young children and older people. ORS helps the body use the water you drink.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Loose, watery stools
Tummy cramps
Feeling sick or vomiting
Fever
Thirst

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Give ORS after each loose stool, a little at a time
Keep eating or breastfeeding
Zinc tablets for children as advised by a doctor
Do not give anti-diarrhoea medicine to young children
Wash hands well

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wash hands with soap
Drink safe water
Cook food well and keep it covered
Breastfeed babies
Give rotavirus vaccine to babies

videos.title: How to wash your hands with soap and water

topics.title: Cholera
short: Cholera causes sudden, very watery diarrhoea.
It spreads in dirty water and can kill within hours.
Rehydration and early care save lives.
goNow: Watery stools like rice water, many times a day
Dry mouth, sunken eyes, dizziness or fainting
Very little urine, cramps in the legs
Go to a hospital now

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Cholera is a bacterial infection spread by contaminated water and food. It causes large amounts of watery diarrhoea and fast dehydration. It is treated with fluids and sometimes antibiotics. Outbreaks happen after floods and where water is unsafe.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Sudden, large watery diarrhoea
Vomiting
Thirst, muscle cramps
Fast heartbeat, sunken eyes
Weakness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Start ORS right away and keep sipping on the way to care
Go to the nearest clinic or hospital
Wash hands well after caring for the sick

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink boiled or treated water
Wash hands with soap
Cook food well
Use a clean toilet and keep water sources clean

topics.title: Hepatitis A
short: Hepatitis A is a liver infection from dirty food or water.
It makes the skin and eyes yellow.
It usually gets better by itself, and a vaccine prevents it.
goNow: Confusion, very sleepy, or bleeding easily
Constant vomiting and cannot drink
Yellow skin and eyes with severe tummy pain

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Hepatitis A is caused by a virus that spreads through food or water with traces of stool, or by close contact. It inflames the liver. Most people recover in a few weeks and then cannot catch it again. It is rarely serious in children but can be in older people.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Yellow skin and eyes
Dark urine, pale stools
Tiredness, loss of appetite
Nausea, tummy pain
Fever

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest
Drink plenty of fluids
Avoid alcohol and ask before taking any medicine
See a doctor for a check

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wash hands with soap
Drink safe water and eat well-cooked food
Get the hepatitis A vaccine

topics.title: Hepatitis B and C
short: Hepatitis B and C are viruses that can harm the liver for years.
Many people feel well and do not know they have it.
A blood test finds it. Hepatitis B can be prevented by vaccine.
goNow: Yellow skin or eyes with confusion
Vomiting blood or black stools
A swollen tummy with fever and tummy pain

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids, and from mother to baby at birth. Hepatitis C spreads mostly through blood. Over time both can cause scarring (cirrhosis) or liver cancer. Treatments can protect the liver, so testing is useful.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Often no signs for years
Tiredness
Yellow skin or eyes
Dark urine
Tummy pain

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor for blood tests and regular liver checks
Avoid alcohol
Ask before taking any herbal or other medicine
Do not share razors or toothbrushes

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Hepatitis B vaccine for all babies and at-risk adults
Do not share needles
Use protection during sex
Test pregnant women

topics.title: Malaria
short: Malaria is spread by the bite of night-biting mosquitoes in some rural and forest areas.
Fever with shivering after travel there needs a blood test at once.
It can be treated, and sleeping under a net prevents it.
goNow: Fever with confusion, fits, or yellow skin
Very hard breathing or very little urine
Heavy bleeding or a child who cannot drink

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Malaria is caused by a parasite carried by the Anopheles mosquito. In the Philippines it is found in some parts of Palawan and a few other places. It is treated with medicine from a health centre. Tell the clinic where you have been.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever with chills and sweats
Headache and muscle pain
Nausea or vomiting
Tiredness
Signs often come in waves

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Get a blood test at the nearest health centre
Take the full course of the medicine given
Rest and drink fluids

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Sleep under a net with insecticide
Use repellent at dusk and night
Ask about preventive medicine before travel to risk areas

topics.title: Measles
short: Measles spreads very easily through the air.
It brings fever and a rash, and can cause pneumonia or harm the brain.
Two doses of vaccine protect children very well.
goNow: Trouble breathing or fast breathing
A child who is very drowsy, has fits or a stiff neck
Cannot drink, or signs of dehydration
Ear pain or eye infection that gets worse

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Measles is a highly catching virus. One sick person can pass it to most unvaccinated people nearby. The rash starts on the face and spreads down. Complications include pneumonia, ear infection and brain swelling. There is no cure, but care at a clinic and vitamin A can help.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever, cough and runny nose
Red, watery eyes
White spots inside the cheeks
A red rash, face first, spreading down
Feeling very unwell

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor or the health centre
Keep the child at home to protect others
Give fluids and keep feeding
Ask about vitamin A as advised by a health worker

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Give the measles vaccine at 9 and 12 months, or as the health centre advises
Catch up on missed doses, adults too
Keep sick children home

topics.title: Chickenpox
short: Chickenpox gives an itchy rash with blisters.
It spreads easily and is milder in children than in adults.
A vaccine prevents it.
goNow: Trouble breathing, or a cough that gets worse
Spots that turn red, swollen, warm or leak pus
A stiff neck, confusion, or very drowsy
Newborns, pregnant women and people with weak immunity need a doctor at once

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Chickenpox is caused by the varicella virus. Itchy blisters appear in waves and then crust over. People can spread it from 1 to 2 days before the rash until all blisters are dry. It can be more serious in newborns, adults, pregnant women and people with weak immunity.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever, tiredness
Itchy red spots that become blisters
New spots for 3 to 5 days
Scabs after a week

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep nails short and clean
Cool baths or wet cloths ease itching
Wear loose cotton clothes
Paracetamol for fever, no aspirin or ibuprofen
Stay home until all blisters are dry

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Chickenpox vaccine (two doses)
Keep away from people with chickenpox if you are not immune
Wash hands

topics.title: Shingles
short: Shingles is a painful rash on one side of the body.
It comes from the chickenpox virus waking up.
See a doctor within 3 days of the rash for best treatment.
goNow: A rash near an eye, or eye pain or changes in vision
A rash with severe pain over the face or ear
Fever with a spreading rash, or weak immunity

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: After chickenpox, the virus stays asleep in the body. Years later it can wake up and cause shingles, often in older adults. The rash usually forms a band on one side. Antiviral medicine works best if started early. The pain can last for weeks.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Burning, tingling or pain on one side
Then a band of blisters
Fever and tiredness
Itching

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor within 3 days
Keep the rash clean and dry, cover loosely
Cool, damp cloths for pain
Avoid contact with babies, pregnant women and people with weak immunity until blisters crust

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Shingles vaccine for adults, ask your doctor
Keep healthy and manage stress

topics.title: Mumps
short: Mumps swells the glands near the ears and cheeks.
It spreads through coughs and sneezes.
The MMR vaccine prevents it.
goNow: Bad headache with stiff neck, vomiting or confusion
Severe tummy pain
A swollen, painful testicle

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Mumps is a virus that makes the glands near the jaw swell. It spreads by coughing and sneezing. It usually clears in about two weeks. Rarely it can cause meningitis or swelling of the testicles or ovaries.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Swollen, painful cheeks or jaw
Fever, headache
Pain when chewing or swallowing
Tiredness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest at home until the swelling is gone, about 5 days
Soft foods and plenty of fluids
Paracetamol for pain or fever
Warm or cool packs on the swollen part

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
MMR vaccine for children
Wash hands
Do not share cups

topics.title: Tetanus
short: Tetanus germs live in soil and enter through wounds.
It causes painful muscle spasms and can kill.
A tetanus shot every 10 years prevents it.
goNow: Stiff jaw or neck, or muscle spasms after a wound
Trouble swallowing or breathing
A deep or dirty wound, and you have not had a tetanus shot in 5 to 10 years

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Tetanus is caused by bacteria in soil, dust and animal waste. They enter through cuts, puncture wounds or burns. The poison causes painful muscle spasms, first in the jaw. Tetanus is preventable with vaccine, and it needs hospital care.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Jaw stiffness (lockjaw)
Stiff neck and muscles
Painful spasms
Trouble swallowing
Fever and sweating

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Wash any wound well with clean water and soap right away
Cover it with a clean cloth
See a clinic for a tetanus shot if the wound is deep, dirty or old

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Tetanus vaccine in childhood and booster every 10 years
Pregnant women get tetanus shots
Clean all wounds well

topics.title: HIV
short: HIV weakens the body's defence against germs.
Medicine lets people with HIV live long, healthy lives.
Testing is free and private at many clinics.
goNow: Within 72 hours of a possible exposure: go to a clinic and ask about PEP
Fever, severe cough or weight loss in a person with HIV
Confusion, severe headache or trouble breathing

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system. It spreads through blood, sex without a condom, and from mother to baby. Medicine called ART keeps the virus down so people stay healthy and do not pass it on. A test at a clinic can tell you your status.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Flu-like illness a few weeks after infection
Often no signs for years
Weight loss, night sweats
Frequent infections
Mouth sores

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take HIV medicine every day, as told
Go to your clinic regularly
Eat well and rest
Use condoms

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Use condoms every time
Do not share needles
PrEP for people at higher risk, ask a clinic
Pregnant women should be tested

topics.title: Sexually transmitted infections
short: STIs spread through sex and often have no signs.
Most can be treated, and some can be cured.
Condoms and regular tests protect you.
goNow: Severe tummy pain with fever
Pain, swelling or a sore in the genital area that gets worse
Pregnant with any signs

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Sexually transmitted infections include chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis, herpes and HPV. Many have no signs for a long time, but can still harm health and spread. Some cause problems in pregnancy or infertility. A clinic can test and treat.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Unusual discharge or smell
Burning when you pass urine
Sores or blisters in the genital area
Pain during sex
Often no signs at all

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a clinic for a private test
Take all medicines as given
Tell your partner so they can be treated
Avoid sex until treated

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Use condoms every time
Get tested with a new partner
HPV vaccine for girls and young women
Limit the number of partners

topics.title: Scabies (galis)
short: Scabies is a skin infestation by tiny mites that cause strong itching.
Itching is worst at night.
It spreads by close contact, so the whole household needs treatment.
goNow: Skin turns red, warm, painful or leaks pus
Fever with spreading redness
A baby or a person with weak immunity

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Scabies is caused by tiny mites that burrow under the skin. It spreads by close skin contact and shared clothes or bedding. It causes strong itching and a rash, often between the fingers, on the wrists and the waist. A doctor can prescribe a cream or tablet that kills the mites.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Strong itching, worse at night
Small red bumps
Thin lines between fingers or on wrists
Scratch marks, sores

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor or health worker for the right cream
Treat everyone in the home at the same time
Wash clothes, towels and bedding in hot water and dry in the sun
Keep nails short

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Avoid sharing clothes, towels and beds
Wash and sun-dry bedding often
Treat family members together

topics.title: Skin fungus (hadhad)
short: Fungus likes warm, damp skin.
It causes itchy, round or scaly patches.
Cream from the pharmacy usually clears it.
goNow: Skin that is very red, swollen, painful or leaks pus
Fever with a spreading rash
A rash on the scalp or nails that does not improve, or in a person with diabetes

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Fungus can grow on skin, nails and scalp. Ringworm makes red, round, scaly patches. Athlete's foot is between the toes. Fungal infections spread by touch, towels and damp floors. They are not caused by worms. Anti-fungal cream usually works in a few weeks.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Itchy, red, scaly rings
Peeling skin between toes
Thick, yellow nails
Hair loss in patches on the scalp

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep the skin clean and dry
Use antifungal cream as directed, past when it looks healed
Wear loose cotton clothes and dry socks
Do not share towels

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Dry well after bathing, especially between toes
Wear slippers in public showers
Change sweaty clothes
Do not share combs or towels

topics.title: Head lice
short: Head lice are tiny insects that live on the scalp.
They spread by close contact, mostly among children.
They are not a sign of being dirty.
goNow: Scalp sores that are red, swollen or leak pus
Fever with swollen neck glands
Lice that stay after proper treatment

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Head lice are small insects that live in hair and feed on the scalp. They spread when heads touch and by sharing combs or caps. They do not cause illness but itch a lot. A pharmacist can suggest a lotion, and a fine comb removes eggs.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Itchy scalp
Tiny white eggs (nits) stuck to hair near the scalp
Small red marks on the scalp or neck
Feeling of something moving

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Use the lotion a pharmacist or doctor suggests
Comb with a fine-toothed comb
Wash combs, caps and bedding in hot water
Check everyone at home

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not share combs, caps or pillows
Tie long hair back at school
Check children's hair weekly

topics.title: Food poisoning
short: Food poisoning comes from food or drink with germs or poisons.
It brings vomiting, diarrhoea and cramps within hours or days.
Most people recover in a day or two with fluids.
goNow: Blood in the stool or vomit
Signs of dehydration: very dry mouth, no urine, dizziness
Fever above 38.5 C, or double vision or trouble speaking
Pregnant, very young, older, or has other illness

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Food poisoning happens when you eat food with germs, or toxins, from poor storage or cooking. It is common in hot weather, after parties and after floods. Seafood, rice left out, raw eggs and unwashed vegetables are common causes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Vomiting
Watery diarrhoea
Tummy cramps
Fever
Weakness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Sip fluids or ORS often in small amounts
Rest the stomach for a few hours then eat plain food like rice or bread
Do not use anti-diarrhoea medicine without a doctor's advice
Wash hands well

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wash hands before cooking and eating
Cook meat, fish and eggs well
Keep cooked food covered and in the fridge
Do not leave rice or food out for hours

topics.title: Intestinal worms
short: Worms in the gut are common in children.
They come from dirty hands, soil and water.
Deworming medicine is safe and often free.
goNow: Severe tummy pain, vomiting and a swollen belly
A worm in the vomit or stool with fever
Very pale, weak child with a swollen tummy

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Roundworm, hookworm, whipworm and pinworm are common gut worms. Eggs spread through soil, unwashed food and dirty hands. They can cause poor growth and anaemia in children. Deworming tablets are given at school and health centres.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Tummy ache
Itching around the bottom at night (pinworm)
Poor appetite or a swollen belly
Tiredness or pale skin
Worms seen in stool

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take deworming medicine as advised by a health worker
Wash hands and trim nails
Wash bedding and underwear in hot water

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wash hands with soap
Wear slippers outside
Wash fruit and vegetables
Use a toilet and drink safe water
Deworm every 6 months as advised

topics.title: Polio
short: Polio is a virus that can cause lasting paralysis.
There is no cure, but the vaccine protects children.
Any child with sudden weak legs needs care at once.
goNow: A child with sudden weak or floppy arms or legs, with or without fever
Trouble breathing or swallowing
Go to the hospital and tell health workers at once

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Polio is a virus that spreads in dirty water and by close contact. Most infected people have no signs, but some are paralysed for life. Polio vaccines given in childhood are very effective. Health workers must be told of every sudden floppy weakness.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever and sore throat
Headache, stiff neck
Weakness in the arms or legs
Muscle pain
Floppy limbs in children

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Go to the hospital if there is sudden weakness
Keep up vaccines

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Polio vaccine on schedule
Catch-up doses for missed children
Wash hands
Use a toilet and safe water

topics.title: Mpox
short: Mpox is a virus that causes a blistering rash.
It spreads through close skin contact.
Most people recover in 2 to 4 weeks.
goNow: Trouble breathing, or confusion
Rash in the eyes or severe pain
Pregnant, a child or a person with weak immunity who has a rash

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Mpox is a virus that spreads by close skin contact, sex, and by touching infected bedding or clothes. It causes fever and a rash with blisters. Most people get better in a few weeks. A vaccine exists for people at higher risk.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever, headache, swollen glands
Rash that turns into blisters
Sores in the mouth or on the genitals
Tiredness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Stay away from others until the rash heals
Do not scratch the blisters
Cover sores with a clean bandage
See a health worker to report and be tested

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Avoid close contact with someone who has the rash
Do not share bedding or towels
Ask about the vaccine if you are at higher risk

topics.title: Sepsis
short: Sepsis is a life-threatening reaction to an infection.
It can start from a small wound, pneumonia or a urine infection.
It needs hospital care at once.
goNow: Fever or low temperature with fast heartbeat and fast breathing
Confusion, very sleepy, or slurred speech
Cold, clammy, blotchy skin, or very little urine
Go to the hospital now

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Sepsis happens when the body's reaction to an infection harms its own organs. Blood pressure can fall. It can start from any infection and needs fast treatment with antibiotics and fluids. Older people, babies and people with weak immunity are at higher risk.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Fever or shivering
Fast heartbeat and fast breathing
Confusion
Very weak or sleepy
Pale, cold or blotchy skin

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
There is no safe home treatment: go to the hospital
Tell staff you worry about sepsis
Treat wounds and infections early

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Clean wounds
Keep vaccines up to date
Treat infections early
Wash hands

topics.title: Schistosomiasis
short: A parasite in water with certain snails can enter through the skin.
It is found in parts of Mindanao, Leyte and Samar.
Tablets given at the health centre treat it.
goNow: Vomiting blood or black stools
A swollen belly with fever, or yellow eyes
Bloody stool or urine that lasts

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Schistosomiasis is caused by worms whose young live in snails in ponds, rice fields and streams. They enter the skin when you wade or wash in the water. Over time they can harm the liver and bowel. A single treatment with praziquantel from the health centre works.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Itchy rash after wading
Fever, tiredness
Tummy pain
Bloody diarrhoea
Swollen belly later

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Go to the rural health unit for testing and treatment
Avoid more contact with infected water

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not wade or swim in water where the snails live
Wear boots in rice fields
Get treated at the yearly drives
Use toilets

topics.title: Filariasis (elephantiasis)
short: Filariasis is caused by tiny worms spread by mosquitoes.
It can cause huge swelling of the leg or other parts.
Yearly tablets in affected areas help stop it.
goNow: Fever with a red, hot, painful swollen leg
Skin cracks that leak or smell, or a wound that will not heal
Trouble breathing or severe pain in the scrotum

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Filariasis is caused by thread-like worms that live in the lymph vessels. Mosquitoes spread them. The damage can lead to swelling called lymphoedema or elephantiasis. Tablets given once a year in affected provinces clear the young worms.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Swollen leg, arm or scrotum
Fever and chills that come and go
Painful lymph glands
Thick, hard skin

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take part in the yearly drug-treatment drive
Wash the swollen part with soap and water daily
Keep it raised when resting
See a health worker for care

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Sleep under a net
Use repellent
Remove standing water where mosquitoes breed

topics.title: Diabetes (type 2)
short: Your body cannot use sugar well, so it builds up in the blood.
Over the years high sugar harms eyes, kidneys, nerves and feet.
Food, activity, medicine and regular checks keep it in range.
goNow: Very sleepy or confused, breathing fast, or fruity-smelling breath
Vomiting that does not stop, or cannot keep fluids down
Sugar very high with extreme thirst and passing a lot of urine
A foot sore with fever or black skin
Shaking, sweating, confusion or passing out (low sugar): give sugar if awake, call 911 if not

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In type 2 diabetes the body does not make enough insulin or does not use it well. Sugar then stays high in the blood. It is often linked to weight, family history and age. It can be controlled and sometimes put into remission, but it needs long-term care.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Very thirsty
Passing urine a lot, especially at night
Tired, blurred vision
Slow-healing sores
Tingling in the feet; many people have no signs

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take medicines or insulin as prescribed
Eat regular meals with less sugar and white rice, more vegetables
Walk after meals if your doctor allows
Check your feet daily
Keep check-ups, eye and kidney tests

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Move 30 minutes on most days
Cut sweet drinks
Get your sugar tested from age 35, or earlier if family has diabetes

videos.title: 10 tips to control diabetes (in Filipino)
How to measure your blood sugar

topics.title: Type 1 diabetes
short: In type 1 diabetes the body makes no insulin.
It often starts in children and young people.
Insulin every day is a must, and never stopped.
goNow: Vomiting, tummy pain, fast breathing, fruity breath (a sign called DKA)
Very sleepy, confused or unconscious
Sugar very high and ketones in the urine

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Type 1 diabetes happens when the body's own defence harms the cells that make insulin. Insulin must be given by injection or pump for life. With good care, children and adults can live full lives. Missing insulin can cause a dangerous emergency called diabetic ketoacidosis.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Very thirsty and hungry
Passing a lot of urine
Weight loss
Tired
Stomach pain or fruity breath if serious

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take insulin exactly as taught
Check sugar as advised
Always carry quick sugar for lows
Never skip insulin when sick
Keep clinic visits

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
It cannot be prevented
Early diagnosis prevents emergencies
Teach family and school what to do for lows

topics.title: Prediabetes
short: Prediabetes means your sugar is above normal but not yet diabetes.
Many people do not know they have it.
Activity and weight loss can turn it back.
goNow: Extreme thirst, passing lots of urine, blurred vision: see a doctor soon
Very sleepy or confused: go to the hospital

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In prediabetes, blood sugar is higher than normal but not high enough for diabetes. Without change, many people get type 2 diabetes within a few years. Losing even a small amount of weight and walking daily can cut the risk a lot.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Usually none
Darker skin on the neck or armpits
Found on a blood test

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Walk 30 minutes most days
Lose a little weight: about 4 to 5 kg if you weigh 70 kg
Eat less sugar and white rice, more vegetables
Re-test your sugar every year

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Move every day
Cut sweet drinks
Do not smoke

topics.title: Low blood sugar
short: Sugar that is too low can make you shaky, sweaty and confused.
It is most common in people who use insulin or some diabetes pills.
Quick sugar fixes it in minutes.
goNow: The person cannot swallow, is very confused, or has a fit
The person passes out: call 911, do not put anything in the mouth
Sugar does not rise after 15 minutes of treatment, or they pass out

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Low blood sugar, usually under 70 mg/dL in a person with diabetes, can come on quickly. Missing a meal, extra exercise, too much insulin or alcohol are common causes. Treat it at once. Unchecked it can cause fits and unconsciousness.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Shaky, sweaty, fast heartbeat
Hunger, headache
Confusion, odd behaviour
Blurry vision
Fainting

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
If awake: give 15 g of quick sugar, such as half a glass of juice or 3 teaspoons of sugar in water
Re-check in 15 minutes and repeat if still low
Then eat a snack or meal
Tell your doctor it happened

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Eat meals on time
Always carry sugar or candy
Check sugar before driving and exercise
Talk to your doctor about medicine doses

videos.title: Diabetic emergency: what to do

topics.title: Diabetic foot care
short: High sugar can numb the feet and slow healing.
A small sore can turn into a serious infection.
Check your feet every day.
goNow: A sore with pus, redness, warmth or a bad smell
Black or blue skin on a toe or foot
Fever with a foot sore, or a hot, swollen foot

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Diabetes can damage nerves and blood vessels in the feet. You may not feel a cut or blister, and it heals slowly. Untreated sores can lead to infection and, in the worst cases, loss of a toe or foot. Daily care prevents most of this.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Numbness or tingling
Burning pain
Dry, cracked skin
Cuts or blisters you did not feel
Colour change

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Look at your feet and between toes every day
Wash with lukewarm water, dry well
Moisturise but not between toes
Wear clean cotton socks and shoes that fit
Never walk barefoot
Do not cut corns yourself

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep sugar in range
Do not smoke
Get a foot check at every visit
Cut toenails straight across

videos.title: WARNING SIGNS! Diabetes-Related Feet Complications
videos.source: Gabay sa Kalusugan - Dr. Gary Sy

topics.title: Diabetes and the eyes
short: High sugar can damage the tiny vessels in the eye.
It can cause blindness, but early signs are silent.
A yearly eye check protects your sight.
goNow: Sudden loss of vision, or a curtain over the vision
Many new floaters or flashes of light
Sudden eye pain or redness with blurred vision

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Diabetic retinopathy is damage to the back of the eye. At first there may be no symptoms. Without treatment it can lead to blindness. Laser or injections can protect sight if found early. Good sugar and blood pressure control slows it.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Often none at first
Blurred or wavy vision
Dark spots (floaters)
Poor night vision
Colours look dull

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Get an eye exam with dilated pupils every year
Keep sugar and blood pressure in range
Do not smoke
Tell your eye doctor you have diabetes

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Control sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol
Yearly eye checks
Stop smoking

topics.title: Thyroid problems
short: The thyroid is a small gland in the neck that controls energy.
It can work too fast or too slow.
A blood test finds it and medicine treats it.
goNow: Trouble breathing or swallowing with a neck swelling
Very fast heartbeat, high fever and confusion
Extreme sleepiness or very cold body and confusion

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The thyroid makes hormones that control how your body uses energy. Underactive thyroid makes you tired, cold and heavy. Overactive thyroid makes you hot, shaky and thin. A swelling in the neck (goitre) can have many causes. Treatment is often a daily tablet or other care.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Under: tiredness, weight gain, constipation, feeling cold
Over: weight loss, racing heart, sweating, anxiety
A lump or swelling in the neck

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take thyroid medicine at the same time each day on an empty stomach
Do not stop without your doctor
Keep blood test follow-ups

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Use iodised salt
See a doctor for a lump in the neck
Do not smoke

topics.title: Overweight and obesity
short: Extra body fat raises the risk of diabetes, high blood pressure and heart disease.
Small changes you can keep work better than crash diets.
Losing even 3 to 5 kg helps your health.
goNow: Chest pain, short of breath, or signs of a stroke
Very high sugar signs: extreme thirst and confusion

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Obesity means having so much body fat that it harms health. A waist over 90 cm in men or 80 cm in women is a warning. It is caused by food, activity, sleep, genes and stress. Slow steady loss is safest.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Often none at first
Short of breath on effort
Snoring
Joint pain
Tiredness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Eat smaller portions of rice and sweets
Swap sweet drinks for water
Walk 30 minutes a day, building up
Sleep 7 hours
Ask for help from a doctor or dietician

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Eat plenty of vegetables
Limit fried and sweet foods
Move every day
Weigh yourself monthly

videos.title: Five a day: eating more fruit and vegetables

topics.title: Metabolic syndrome
short: A group of problems: a big waist, high blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol.
Together they raise the risk of heart disease and diabetes.
Healthy living can reverse it.
goNow: Chest pain, signs of stroke, or very high sugar signs: go to the hospital

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Metabolic syndrome means you have several of these together: a large waist, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high triglycerides and low HDL cholesterol. It raises the chance of diabetes, heart attack and stroke.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Large waist
Often no signs
Found on checks of blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Walk daily
Cut sweet drinks and fried food
Lose a little weight
Take any prescribed medicines

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Be active
Eat plenty of vegetables
Do not smoke

topics.title: Diabetes in pregnancy
short: Some women get high sugar for the first time in pregnancy.
It usually goes away after birth, but raises the risk of later diabetes.
Good control protects mother and baby.
goNow: Baby moves much less than usual
Very thirsty, vomiting, fast breathing or confusion
Headache, vision changes or swelling of the face

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Gestational diabetes is high blood sugar that starts in pregnancy. It can make the baby grow large and cause problems at birth. A sugar test between weeks 24 and 28 checks for it. Food, activity and sometimes insulin keep it under control.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Often none
Very thirsty
Passing more urine
Tiredness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Follow the meal plan from your doctor or dietician
Walk after meals
Check sugar as advised
Keep all prenatal visits
Test sugar again 6 to 12 weeks after birth

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight before pregnancy
Be active
Get a sugar test in pregnancy

topics.title: Chronic kidney disease
short: Your kidneys slowly lose the power to clean the blood.
Diabetes and high blood pressure are the top causes.
Early care can slow it down, but it cannot be felt early.
goNow: Very little or no urine, or swelling of the face and legs that gets worse
Trouble breathing, or chest pain
Confusion, vomiting that will not stop, or fits

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The kidneys clean waste and extra water from the blood. In chronic kidney disease they slowly lose this power over months or years. There is often no sign until late. Controlling blood pressure and sugar, a kidney-friendly diet and avoiding certain painkillers protect what is left.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Often none early
Swollen feet or puffy eyes
Tired, poor appetite
Foamy urine
Itchy skin

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take blood pressure and sugar medicines as told
Avoid ibuprofen and similar painkillers and herbal remedies unless your doctor agrees
Eat less salt
Ask for a diet plan, with limits on some foods
Get blood and urine tests regularly

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Control blood pressure and diabetes
Do not smoke
Drink enough water
Get yearly urine and blood tests if you are at risk

videos.title: Mayo Clinic Minute: Understanding chronic kidney disease

topics.title: Kidney failure and dialysis
short: When the kidneys fail, a machine or a transplant must do their work.
Dialysis cleans the blood several times a week.
PhilHealth helps cover dialysis sessions.
goNow: Missed dialysis and now short of breath, swollen or very tired
Chest pain, very fast or slow heartbeat, or muscle weakness
Signs of infection around the dialysis catheter: fever, redness, pus

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In kidney failure the kidneys work at less than 15 of every 100 as normal. Waste and water build up. Treatment is dialysis (a machine cleans the blood) or a kidney transplant. Dialysis works only if you attend every session and follow the diet and fluid limits.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Very tired and weak
Nausea, poor appetite
Swelling
Short of breath
Itchy skin

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Never miss a dialysis session
Follow limits on water, salt, potassium and phosphate
Keep the access site clean
Take medicines as told

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Control diabetes and blood pressure
Avoid unneeded painkillers
Treat kidney disease early

topics.title: Kidney stones
short: Stones are hard lumps that form in the kidney from salts.
They cause sudden, very bad pain in the side.
Drinking lots of water helps pass them and prevents more.
goNow: Fever or chills with side pain
Cannot pass urine, or blood in urine with pain
Pain so bad you cannot sit still, or constant vomiting

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Kidney stones form when minerals in the urine clump together. Small stones can pass on their own with fluids and pain relief. Bigger stones may need a procedure. Dehydration is a common cause, so heat and sweating matter.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Sharp pain in the side or back, can move to the groin
Blood in the urine
Burning or urgent urination
Nausea or vomiting

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Drink plenty of water, enough to pass pale urine
Take pain relief as the doctor advises
Strain your urine if told, and keep the stone for testing
Follow-up with the doctor

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink 2 to 3 litres of water daily
Eat less salt
Eat more fruit and vegetables
Limit animal protein

topics.title: Urine infection (UTI)
short: A UTI is an infection of the bladder or kidneys.
It burns when you pass urine.
Antibiotics from a doctor clear it, and fluids help.
goNow: Fever and chills or pain in your back or side
Blood in the urine, or vomiting
Pregnant, a child, or a man with these signs
Confusion in an older person with a urine infection

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A urinary tract infection is caused by bacteria, usually in the bladder. It is more common in women. If it spreads to the kidneys it can be serious. A doctor may test the urine. Antibiotics clear it, and you must finish the course.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Burning when passing urine
Passing small amounts often
Cloudy or bad-smelling urine
Lower tummy pain
Fever or back pain if the kidneys are involved

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Drink plenty of water
See a doctor for a urine test and antibiotics
Finish all the antibiotics
Do not hold urine for long

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink enough water
Pass urine after sex
Wipe front to back
Do not hold in urine
Keep the genital area clean and dry

topics.title: Bladder leaks
short: Many people leak urine, and it can usually be helped.
Do not hide it: treatments exist.
Pelvic muscle exercises help most people.
goNow: Cannot pass urine at all
Blood in the urine, fever or pain
Sudden weakness of the legs with leaks

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Leaking urine is common, mostly in women after childbirth and in older people. Types include leaks when coughing (stress), a sudden strong need (urge) and a full bladder that overflows. A doctor can find the cause and help.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Leaks when coughing, sneezing or lifting
A sudden strong need to go
Frequent trips to the toilet
Getting up many times at night

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Do pelvic floor (Kegel) exercises daily
Limit coffee, tea and alcohol
Go to the toilet on a schedule
Keep a healthy weight
See a doctor

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Do pelvic floor exercises after pregnancy
Treat constipation
Do not smoke

topics.title: Prostate problems
short: The prostate can grow with age and block the flow of urine.
This is common and not usually cancer.
See a doctor for a slow stream or getting up at night.
goNow: Cannot pass urine at all
Fever with burning urination or pain
Blood in the urine, or bone pain
