sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The prostate is a gland below the bladder in men. With age it often grows (benign prostatic hyperplasia) and presses on the urine tube. This causes a weak stream and urgency. Medicine or surgery can help. A doctor may check for prostate cancer with an exam and a blood test.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Weak or slow urine stream
Needing to go often, especially at night
Dribbling after finishing
Feeling the bladder is not empty

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Limit fluids and coffee in the evening
Do not hold urine
Take medicines as prescribed
Go for check-ups

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Stay active
Keep a healthy weight
Talk to your doctor about prostate checks after 50

topics.title: Fatty liver
short: Extra fat stored in the liver is very common.
Most people feel nothing.
Weight loss and less sugar can reverse it.
goNow: Yellow skin or eyes with tummy swelling
Vomiting blood or black stools
Confusion or very sleepy

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Fatty liver means too much fat builds up in the liver. It is linked to being overweight, diabetes, high cholesterol, and sometimes alcohol. In time it can cause inflammation and scarring. It is often found on an ultrasound. Lifestyle changes work best.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Usually none
Tiredness
Mild ache in the upper right tummy
Found on a scan or blood test

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Lose weight slowly
Cut sugary drinks, sweets and fried food
Avoid alcohol
Move 30 minutes on most days
Keep sugar and cholesterol in check

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Limit sugar and alcohol
Stay active
Get a hepatitis B vaccine

topics.title: Cirrhosis
short: Cirrhosis is deep scarring of the liver.
Long-term alcohol and hepatitis B or C are common causes.
Stopping the cause protects what is left.
goNow: Vomiting blood or black stools
Confusion, sleepiness or odd behaviour
A swollen tummy with fever or pain

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Years of damage turn healthy liver into scar tissue. The liver cannot clean the blood or make proteins well. Treating hepatitis, stopping alcohol and watching diet can slow it. Some people need a transplant.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Tiredness and weakness
Yellow skin and eyes
Swollen tummy and legs
Easy bruising
Itchy skin

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Do not drink alcohol
Take medicines as told and ask before any herbal remedies
Eat less salt
Keep check-ups

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Hepatitis B vaccine
Limit alcohol
Treat hepatitis C
Keep a healthy weight

topics.title: Gallstones
short: Gallstones are hard lumps in the gallbladder.
They can cause sudden pain after a fatty meal.
Surgery may be needed if they cause trouble.
goNow: Pain in the upper right tummy for more than 5 hours
Fever and chills, or yellow skin or eyes
Vomiting that will not stop

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The gallbladder stores bile that helps digest fat. Stones can form and block the flow. This causes a sharp pain, often after eating fatty food. Women, those who are overweight and those over 40 have a higher risk.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Sudden pain in the upper right tummy or middle
Pain going to the right shoulder
Nausea, vomiting
Pain after fatty meals

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Eat small, low-fat meals
Avoid fried and fatty food
See a doctor for an ultrasound
Keep a healthy weight without crash diets

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Eat more fibre
Avoid very fast weight loss

topics.title: Heartburn and reflux
short: Stomach acid comes up into the food pipe and burns.
Smaller meals and not lying down after eating help.
Chest pain is not always heartburn.
goNow: Chest pain with sweating, shortness of breath or pain in the arm or jaw
Vomiting blood, black stools, or trouble swallowing
Weight loss without trying

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: GERD happens when the muscle at the end of the food pipe lets acid flow back up. It causes a burning in the chest after meals. Large meals, being overweight, smoking, coffee and lying down soon after eating make it worse. Antacids may help; if it is frequent see a doctor.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Burning in the chest, mostly after eating
Sour taste in the mouth
Cough at night
Hoarse voice

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Eat smaller meals and stop 3 hours before bed
Raise the head of the bed
Limit coffee, alcohol, spicy and fatty food
Do not smoke
Lose weight if overweight

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Do not smoke
Avoid big, late meals

topics.title: Stomach ulcer
short: An ulcer is a sore in the stomach or gut lining.
A germ called H. pylori and some painkillers cause most.
Medicine heals it, and the germ can be cleared.
goNow: Vomiting blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds
Black, tarry or bloody stools
Sudden, severe tummy pain

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A peptic ulcer is an open sore in the lining of the stomach or the first part of the gut. Most are caused by H. pylori or by painkillers such as ibuprofen. Medicine to lower acid and kill the germ heals ulcers. Untreated, they can bleed.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Burning pain in the upper tummy, often between meals or at night
Bloating, feeling full
Nausea
Weight loss
Often eased by food or antacids

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
See a doctor for treatment and test for H. pylori
Avoid ibuprofen, aspirin and similar painkillers unless your doctor says
Stop smoking and alcohol
Eat regular meals

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Use painkillers sparingly
Do not smoke
Wash hands and eat well-cooked food

topics.title: Constipation
short: Constipation is hard, dry stools or going less than three times a week.
Fibre, water and moving usually help.
See a doctor if it is new, painful or lasts weeks.
goNow: Blood in the stool, or black stools
Severe tummy pain and swelling with vomiting
Weight loss without trying

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Constipation is common and often caused by too little fibre or water, not enough movement, or some medicines. It usually gets better with food and fluids. If you have new constipation after age 50, it should be checked.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Hard, dry stools
Straining
Bloating or tummy pain
Feeling you cannot empty fully

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Eat more vegetables, fruit, oats and whole grains
Drink 6 to 8 glasses of water
Walk daily
Go to the toilet when you feel the urge
Ask a pharmacist about gentle laxatives for short use

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Fibre, water and movement
Do not ignore the urge
Ask your doctor if a medicine causes it

topics.title: Hemorrhoids (almoranas)
short: Swollen veins around the bottom can itch, hurt or bleed.
They are common and often get better with care.
Blood in the stool should always be checked once.
goNow: Heavy bleeding, dizziness or fainting
Black stools, or blood mixed in the stool
Severe pain or a hard, painful lump

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Hemorrhoids are swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus. They are caused by straining, constipation, pregnancy and sitting long. Bright red blood on the paper is a common sign, but other conditions can look the same, so see a doctor the first time.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Bright red blood after a bowel movement
Itching or pain around the anus
A soft lump
Mucus

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Eat more fibre and water
Do not strain or sit long on the toilet
Warm sitz baths
Ask a pharmacist about creams
Keep the area clean

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Treat constipation
Do not strain
Exercise
Lose weight if overweight

topics.title: Appendicitis
short: Appendicitis is a swollen, infected appendix.
It causes pain that moves to the lower right tummy.
It needs urgent care.
goNow: Tummy pain that gets worse, mostly on the lower right
Pain with fever, vomiting or a hard belly
Pain when you move, cough or press and let go
Go to the hospital now. Do not take laxatives.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The appendix is a small tube on the right of the lower belly. If it becomes blocked and infected, it can burst. Surgery is the usual treatment. Do not eat or drink and do not take painkillers or laxatives while you go to get help.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Pain near the belly button that moves to the lower right
Loss of appetite
Nausea or vomiting
Fever
Pain when moving or coughing

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Go to a hospital now
Do not eat or drink
Do not take laxatives

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
It cannot be prevented
Get care early for belly pain that is getting worse

topics.title: Irritable bowel (IBS)
short: IBS causes cramps, bloating and changes in stool without damage to the gut.
Stress and some foods make it worse.
It is long-term, and often manageable.
goNow: Blood in the stool, or weight loss
Severe pain that wakes you at night
New signs after age 50

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Irritable bowel syndrome is a common gut problem with cramps and changes in bowel habits (diarrhoea, constipation or both). Doctors find no damage in the bowel, but it can be painful. Finding your trigger foods and managing stress help.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Cramping pain
Bloating and wind
Diarrhoea, constipation or both
Mucus in stool
Better after passing stool

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep a food diary to find triggers
Eat regular meals
Add fibre slowly
Reduce stress with walking and breathing
See a doctor

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Manage stress
Sleep well
Avoid foods that bring on attacks

topics.title: Depression
short: Depression is more than feeling sad: it lasts for weeks and affects daily life.
It is an illness, not weakness, and it can be treated.
Talking to someone and sometimes medicine help.
goNow: Thoughts of ending your life or hurting yourself: call the NCMH crisis hotline 1553 or 911 now
Hearing or seeing things that are not there
You cannot care for yourself, or a person you know says they want to die

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Depression is a medical illness that causes ongoing sadness or loss of interest for two weeks or more. It can affect sleep, appetite, energy and thinking. It is common, and more common after loss, illness or hard times. Counselling, medicine or both work well for most people.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Low mood most of the day
Loss of interest in things you liked
Sleeping too little or too much
Tired, poor appetite or eating more
Feeling worthless or guilty
Trouble thinking

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Talk to someone you trust
Keep a daily routine, sleep and eat regularly
Take a short walk in daylight
Avoid alcohol
See a doctor, health worker or counsellor

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Stay connected with family and friends
Move your body
Ask for help early
Limit alcohol

videos.title: Lusog-Isip: looking after your mental health

topics.title: Anxiety
short: Anxiety is strong worry or fear that does not go away.
It can cause a racing heart, shaking and poor sleep.
Slow breathing, talking therapy and sometimes medicine help.
goNow: Chest pain, or an attack you think may be a heart attack
Thoughts of hurting yourself: call the NCMH hotline 1553 or 911
Cannot breathe, or faint

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Everyone feels worried at times. Anxiety disorders cause worry, fear or panic that is strong, lasts a long time and gets in the way of life. They are common and treatable. A doctor can check that nothing else, like a thyroid problem, is causing the signs.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Constant worry
Restless or on edge
Racing heart, sweating, shaking
Trouble sleeping
Tight muscles, stomach upset
Avoiding places or people

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Breathe in for 4, out for 6, a few minutes
Walk or stretch daily
Cut down coffee and alcohol
Talk to a trusted person
Ask a doctor or counsellor for help

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Sleep and exercise regularly
Limit caffeine and alcohol
Manage stress
Ask for support early

videos.title: Steps for Stress: a breathing exercise

topics.title: Panic attacks
short: A panic attack is a sudden wave of intense fear.
It feels frightening, but it passes, usually within 20 minutes.
Slow breathing helps, and treatment can stop them coming back.
goNow: Chest pain that may be a heart attack: go to the hospital to be safe the first time
Thoughts of ending your life: call 1553 or 911

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A panic attack is a rush of fear with strong body signs: pounding heart, chest tightness, shaking, a feeling of unreality. It peaks within minutes and then passes. If attacks keep coming, or you fear the next one, it is called panic disorder, and treatment works.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Racing heart
Chest tightness
Shortness of breath
Dizziness, tingling
Feeling you may die or lose control

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Sit, breathe in slowly for 4, out for 6
Tell yourself: this will pass
Name 5 things you can see
Avoid caffeine and alcohol
See a doctor if it keeps happening

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Regular sleep and exercise
Limit coffee
Learn breathing and relaxing skills
Therapy helps

topics.title: Dementia and Alzheimer's
short: Dementia is a loss of memory and thinking that gets in the way of daily life.
It is not a normal part of getting old.
Early checks, a routine and caring support help families cope.
goNow: Sudden confusion, speech trouble or weakness: this could be a stroke, go to hospital now
A person who wanders and is lost, or unsafe at home
Hurting self or others, or severe agitation

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Dementia is a group of illnesses, including Alzheimer's disease, that slowly harm memory, thinking and behaviour. It is more common with age, but it is not a normal part of ageing. There is no cure, but care and some medicines can help. Some memory loss has other causes that can be treated, so see a doctor.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Forgetting recent events and repeating questions
Getting lost in familiar places
Trouble with words and daily tasks
Changes in mood or personality
Confusion about time and place

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep a calm routine
Use notes, labels and a calendar
Keep the home safe: night lights, no clutter, locked stove
Keep active and social
Caregivers need rest and support too

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Control blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol
Stay active, mentally and physically
Do not smoke
Treat hearing loss
Stay connected with others

videos.title: Caring for someone with Alzheimer's or dementia (in Filipino)

topics.title: Trouble sleeping
short: Trouble falling or staying asleep for weeks needs attention.
Habits and a calm bedtime help most people.
Sleeping pills are a short-term answer at best.
goNow: Falling asleep while driving or at work
Thoughts of hurting yourself
Loud snoring with choking at night

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Insomnia is trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking too early, and feeling tired in the day. Stress, worry, pain, caffeine, screens and some medicines can cause it. Good sleep habits are the first treatment.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Lying awake at night
Waking often or too early
Tired in the day
Poor focus
Irritable

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Go to bed and get up at the same time each day
Keep the room dark, cool and quiet
No coffee after noon, no alcohol before bed
Put phones away an hour before bed
Get out of bed if you cannot sleep for 20 minutes

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Regular sleep time
Daylight and exercise in the day
Limit naps
Do not use alcohol to sleep

topics.title: Stress
short: Stress is the body's reaction to pressure.
A little can help, but too much for too long harms health.
Rest, movement and talking to someone ease it.
goNow: Chest pain, or trouble breathing
Thoughts of ending your life: call 1553 or 911
Violence or fear of hurting someone

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Stress is how your body and mind respond to hard events like money worries, illness, work or family problems. Short-term stress can be useful. Long-term stress can lead to poor sleep, headaches, high blood pressure and low mood.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Tense muscles, headache
Poor sleep
Worry and irritability
Upset stomach
Eating or drinking more

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Slow breathing: in for 4, out for 6
Walk or stretch every day
Talk to a family member, friend or priest
Make a short to-do list and do one thing
Take breaks, rest

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Plan your day
Say no sometimes
Sleep and eat well
Stay in touch with people
Limit alcohol

topics.title: Thoughts of suicide: how to help
short: Thinking of suicide is a sign of deep pain, not weakness.
Help works, and the feeling can pass.
If you or someone is in danger now, call 911 or the NCMH hotline 1553.
goNow: Someone says they want to die or has a plan: stay with them and call 1553 or 911
Remove anything that could be used for harm
Go to the nearest emergency room if you are in danger

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Many people have thoughts of suicide at some point, often when pain feels too big. It is not selfish or weak. Talking to someone caring and getting professional help can bring relief. Asking directly about suicide does not plant the idea. It can save a life.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Talking about death or being a burden
Giving away things
Withdrawing from people
Big mood changes
Using more alcohol or drugs

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Ask: are you thinking about ending your life?
Listen without judging
Stay with them, and remove means of harm
Call 1553 (NCMH) or 911
Follow up after the crisis

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep connected
Treat depression
Limit alcohol
Store medicines and sharp tools safely
Seek help early

topics.title: Bipolar disorder
short: Bipolar disorder causes big swings between high energy and deep lows.
It can be managed with medicine and support.
Stopping medicine suddenly can bring a relapse.
goNow: Thoughts of suicide: call 1553 or 911
Not sleeping for days with wild ideas, or risky behaviour
Hearing voices or seeing things

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Bipolar disorder involves episodes of mania (very high energy, little sleep, fast talk, risky choices) and depression. Moods can last days or weeks. Medicine and talking therapy help people keep steady. Family support makes a big difference.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Mania: little need for sleep, racing thoughts, spending sprees
Depression: low mood, tiredness, hopelessness
Moods that swing over weeks

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take medicine as prescribed
Keep a regular sleep time
Avoid alcohol and drugs
Learn your early warning signs
Keep regular check-ups

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Take medicine every day
Keep routines
Reduce stress
Seek help at the first signs

topics.title: Schizophrenia
short: Schizophrenia is a long-term illness that changes how a person thinks and perceives.
It is a brain illness, not a curse or a personal failing.
Medicine and family support help people live well.
goNow: Thoughts of hurting self or others
Not eating, drinking or sleeping for days, or cannot care for self
Very frightened or aggressive

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Schizophrenia is an illness that can cause hearing voices, false beliefs, disorganised thinking and withdrawal. It often starts in young adults. Treatment with medicine, therapy and family support works. Stopping medicine without advice often leads to a relapse. People with this illness deserve respect and care.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Hearing voices
Strong, false beliefs
Confused speech
Withdrawn, flat feelings
Neglecting self-care

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Support them in taking medicine
Keep a calm, kind routine at home
Avoid arguing about the beliefs
Go to follow-up visits
Avoid alcohol and drugs

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Early care limits the harm
Avoid drug use
Family support and a regular routine help

topics.title: Drinking too much alcohol
short: Alcohol harms the liver, heart, brain and family life.
It is hard to stop alone, and help is available.
Sudden stopping after heavy use can be dangerous.
goNow: Shaking, sweating, seeing things or fits after stopping alcohol
Vomiting blood, black stools or yellow eyes
Confusion, or a person who cannot be woken

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Alcohol use disorder means you cannot stop or control drinking even when it causes harm. Over time it can damage the liver, heart, brain and mood. If you drink every day, do not stop suddenly without a doctor's help, because withdrawal can be dangerous.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Drinking more or longer than planned
Cravings
Trouble at work or home
Needing more to feel the effect
Shaking or sweats when you do not drink

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Tell a trusted person and a doctor
Do not stop suddenly if you drink heavily every day
Counselling and medicine can help
Avoid places where you drink
Join a support group

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Limit alcohol or avoid it
Never drink and drive
Eat before drinking
Do not drink during pregnancy

topics.title: Drug use and addiction
short: Addiction is a health problem that can be treated.
Shabu and other drugs harm the brain and heart.
Help is available without shame.
goNow: Chest pain, fits, hard breathing or unconsciousness after using
Violent behaviour, or a person who is a danger to self or others
An overdose: call 911 now

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Drug addiction is when a person keeps using despite harm. Drugs such as shabu (methamphetamine) can cause heart problems, strokes, fits and serious mental illness. Recovery is possible with counselling, support, family and sometimes medicine.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Strong cravings
Using more over time
Neglecting work and family
Secretive, changes in sleep and mood
Withdrawal sickness when stopping

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Talk to a doctor, counsellor or the barangay health worker
Join a community-based recovery programme
Remove drugs from the home
Support, not blame

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Talk with children about drugs
Keep busy with healthy activities
Treat depression and stress early

topics.title: Headache
short: Most headaches are harmless and ease with rest and water.
Some headaches are warning signs and need care at once.
A "worst headache of my life" is an emergency.
goNow: Sudden, severe headache that is the worst you have ever had
Headache with stiff neck, fever, confusion, rash or fits
Weakness, numbness, trouble speaking or seeing, or after a head injury
Headache that wakes you or is getting worse over weeks

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Tension headaches from stress and tight muscles are the most common. Others come from dehydration, lack of sleep, eye strain, colds, high blood pressure, and migraines. Painkillers used too often can make headaches worse.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Tight band or pressure
Pain behind the eyes
Sore neck and shoulders
Sensitivity to light or sound (migraine)

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Drink water and rest in a quiet, dark room
Paracetamol may help (follow the pack)
Cold or warm cloth on the head or neck
Check your blood pressure
Do not use painkillers more than 2 days a week

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Sleep regularly
Drink enough water
Take breaks from screens
Manage stress
Keep a headache diary

topics.title: Migraine
aka: sakit ng ulo sa isang bahagi
short: A migraine is a throbbing headache, often with sickness and sensitivity to light.
Triggers like stress and missed meals can start it.
Medicine and a plan from a doctor can help a lot.
goNow: Weakness, speech trouble or vision loss that does not clear in an hour
Sudden worst headache of your life
Headache with fever, stiff neck or confusion

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A migraine is a strong headache, often on one side, that throbs and can last hours to days. It can come with nausea, vomiting and sensitivity to light and sound. Some people see zigzag lights first (aura). Common triggers are stress, hunger, poor sleep, bright light and some foods.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Throbbing pain, often on one side
Nausea or vomiting
Light and sound hurt
Zigzag lights before the pain

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Lie down in a dark, quiet room
Take your migraine medicine at the first sign
Drink water, eat small meals
Keep a diary to find triggers
Cool cloth on the forehead

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Regular sleep and meals
Limit stress and known triggers
Ask your doctor about preventive medicine

topics.title: Epilepsy and seizures
short: Epilepsy causes repeated seizures from sudden bursts in the brain.
Most people are well controlled with medicine.
Learn how to help someone during a seizure.
goNow: A seizure that lasts more than 5 minutes
Seizures one after another, or the person does not wake up
First seizure, or injury, or trouble breathing afterwards
Call 911 for any of these

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A seizure is a burst of uncontrolled electrical activity in the brain. Epilepsy means having seizures again and again. Medicine controls them in most people. Do not put anything in the person's mouth. Keep them safe until it ends.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Stiff body, jerking
Staring, not responding
Falling, loss of awareness
Confusion after

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Move hard things away and cushion the head
Turn the person on their side when jerking stops
Time the seizure
Stay with them until awake
Do not hold them down or put anything in the mouth

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Take medicine every day
Sleep well
Avoid alcohol
Wear a helmet when cycling
Do not drive until your doctor agrees

topics.title: Parkinson's disease
short: Parkinson's disease slowly causes shaking, stiffness and slow movement.
Medicines can ease the signs for years.
Falls are the biggest danger, so keep the home safe.
goNow: A fall with injury
Trouble swallowing or choking when eating
Confusion or hallucinations that are new

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Parkinson's disease is caused by loss of brain cells that make dopamine, a chemical that helps control movement. It is more common in older people. Medicines such as levodopa help. Exercise, balance training and a safe home help people stay independent.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Hand tremor at rest
Stiff muscles
Slow movement and small handwriting
Shuffling steps
Stooped posture

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take medicines on time
Do daily walking and stretches
Clear loose rugs and cords, add handrails
Eat fibre and drink water
Keep follow-up

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Stay active
Fall-proof the home
It is not known how to prevent it

topics.title: Dizziness and vertigo
short: Dizziness has many causes, most not serious.
Spinning (vertigo) often comes from the inner ear.
Sudden dizziness with other signs can be a stroke.
goNow: Dizziness with weakness, numbness, drooping face, or speech trouble
Dizziness with chest pain or a fast, uneven heartbeat
Dizziness with a severe headache, fainting or double vision

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Dizziness can be feeling faint or feeling that the room is spinning (vertigo). Common causes are low blood pressure, dehydration, medicines and inner ear problems. The ear problem called BPPV is treatable with head movements done by a trained person.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Spinning feeling
Lightheaded
Unsteady walking
Nausea
Dizzy when turning in bed

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Sit or lie down until it passes
Drink water
Get up slowly
Avoid driving
See a doctor if repeated

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Stay hydrated
Review medicines with your doctor
Rise slowly
Keep blood pressure and sugar in check

topics.title: Forgetfulness
short: Mild forgetfulness is common with age.
Memory problems that get worse or affect daily life need a check.
Some causes can be treated.
goNow: Sudden confusion, trouble speaking or weakness: go to the hospital
A person who gets lost or is unsafe alone

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Forgetting names or where you put keys can be normal. Forgetting how to do familiar tasks, getting lost or repeating questions over and over is not. Low vitamins, thyroid problems, depression, poor sleep, medicines and infections can all affect memory, and some of these can be treated.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Misplacing things often
Repeating the same question
Trouble following a conversation
Getting lost on a familiar road

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Use lists, a calendar and a pill box
Keep a routine
Sleep well and stay active
Ask your doctor to check medicines and blood tests

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep active and social
Control blood pressure and sugar
Do not smoke
Limit alcohol

topics.title: Arthritis of the joints (osteoarthritis)
short: The cushion in a joint wears down over the years.
Knees, hips and hands are the usual places.
Moving gently, a healthy weight and pain relief help.
goNow: A hot, red, swollen joint with fever
A joint that cannot be moved or bear weight after a fall
Sudden severe swelling in one joint

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Osteoarthritis is the most common arthritis. The smooth cartilage that cushions a joint slowly wears away. The joint becomes stiff and painful, mostly in the knees, hips, spine and hands. It is more common with age, past injury and extra weight.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Joint pain that worsens with use
Stiffness in the morning, less than 30 minutes
Swelling or bony lumps
Cracking sounds
Less movement

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep moving: walking, swimming, gentle cycling
Lose weight if overweight
Warm packs for stiffness, cold for swelling
Paracetamol for pain, or as your doctor advises
Wear supportive shoes

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Stay active
Protect joints from injury
Strengthen leg muscles

topics.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
short: The body's defence attacks the lining of the joints.
Joints in both hands or feet swell and stiffen.
Early treatment prevents lasting damage.
goNow: A red, hot joint with fever
Fever with chest pain, or new shortness of breath
Sudden loss of function in a hand or foot

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune illness. The immune system attacks the joint lining, causing swelling and pain on both sides of the body. Without treatment it can damage the joints. Medicines called DMARDs slow the damage, so see a doctor early.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Swollen, warm joints on both sides
Morning stiffness for more than an hour
Tiredness
Low fever
Small hand and foot joints first

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take your medicines exactly as told
Gentle movement and rest in balance
Warm showers for stiffness
Do not smoke
Keep follow-up blood tests

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Do not smoke
Treat early
Keep a healthy weight

topics.title: Gout
short: Gout is a sudden, very painful swelling of a joint, often the big toe.
It is caused by too much uric acid in the blood.
Diet, water and medicine can prevent attacks.
goNow: Fever with a hot, red, swollen joint
A joint that is red, hot and extremely painful and you cannot move it
Gout with very little urine, or severe back pain

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Gout happens when uric acid forms sharp crystals in a joint. Attacks start suddenly, often at night. Triggers include alcohol (beer), organ meats, seafood, sweet drinks and dehydration. Medicines can lower uric acid over the long term.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Sudden severe pain in one joint, often the big toe
Swelling, redness and warmth
Even a bedsheet hurts
Attacks last days

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest and raise the joint
Cold packs help
Drink plenty of water
Take the medicine your doctor gave for attacks
Limit alcohol, organ meats, shellfish and sweet drinks

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Drink water
Limit beer, organ meats, sardines and soft drinks
Take uric-acid-lowering medicine if your doctor prescribes

videos.title: Gout and Heart Disease
videos.source: Gabay sa Kalusugan - Dr. Gary Sy

topics.title: Weak bones (osteoporosis)
short: Bones become thin and easy to break.
Many people find out only after a fracture.
Calcium, vitamin D, activity and sometimes medicine protect bones.
goNow: Sudden back pain after lifting or a small fall
A fall followed by hip pain and unable to stand
Loss of height or a rounded back

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In osteoporosis the bones lose density and become weak. A small fall can then break a hip, wrist or spine. It is common in women after menopause and in older men. A bone density scan (DEXA) shows how strong bones are.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Usually none until a fracture
Loss of height
Stooped back
Back pain from a spine fracture

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Eat food rich in calcium: dilis, tofu, milk, malunggay, leafy greens
Sit in morning sun for a short time for vitamin D
Walk or do light weight exercise
Make the home fall-safe
Take medicine as prescribed

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Calcium and vitamin D
Weight-bearing exercise
Do not smoke
Limit alcohol
Bone scan after 65, or earlier if at risk

topics.title: Back pain
short: Most back pain gets better in a few weeks.
Staying gently active heals faster than bed rest.
A few signs mean see a doctor at once.
goNow: Loss of control of urine or stool, or numbness in the groin
Weakness or numbness in both legs
Back pain after a fall or accident, or with fever
Pain that wakes you at night with weight loss

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Most back pain comes from strained muscles or joints, often after lifting or sitting long. It usually improves within weeks. Rarely it is a sign of a serious problem, like a pinched nerve, infection or fracture, so know the warning signs.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Dull ache or stiffness
Sharp pain when moving
Pain that spreads to the buttock or leg
Better with rest, worse with lifting

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep moving gently, short walks
Avoid bed rest for more than a day or two
Warm packs
Paracetamol if needed
Lift with your knees, not your back

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Exercise your core and legs
Keep a healthy weight
Lift properly
Sit with a supported back
Do not smoke

topics.title: Neck and shoulder pain
short: Most neck pain is from strain and poor posture.
It often eases in days to weeks.
A stiff neck with fever or severe headache is an emergency.
goNow: Stiff neck with fever, headache and confusion
Weakness or numbness in the arms
Neck pain after a fall or accident

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Sitting hunched over a phone or desk, sleeping in a bad position or a sudden jerk can strain the neck muscles. A pinched nerve can cause pain down the arm. Most cases settle with simple care.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Stiff, sore neck
Pain turning the head
Headache from the neck
Shoulder tightness
Tingling in the arm if a nerve is pinched

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Warm pack or warm shower
Gentle neck stretches
Keep moving
Fix your pillow height
Paracetamol if needed

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep your screen at eye level
Take breaks every 30 minutes
Sleep with a supportive pillow
Strengthen neck and shoulders

topics.title: Knee pain
short: Knee pain is common with age, weight and activity.
Rest, ice and gentle strength exercises help most.
A knee that locks, gives way or swells fast needs a check.
goNow: A hot, red, swollen knee with fever
Cannot bear weight, or the knee looks out of shape
Pain after a fall with a pop or sudden swelling

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The knee carries your whole body weight. Pain can come from arthritis, a sprain, a torn cartilage or overuse. Stronger thigh muscles, a healthy weight and the right shoes ease stress on the knee.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Pain on stairs or squatting
Stiffness after sitting
Swelling
Clicking, locking, or giving way

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest the knee, raise it and use ice for swelling for 15 minutes at a time
Use a cane in the opposite hand if needed
Gentle thigh exercises
Lose extra weight
Wear supportive shoes

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep a healthy weight
Strengthen leg muscles
Warm up before exercise
Wear proper shoes

topics.title: Broken bone
short: A broken bone causes pain, swelling and sometimes a bent shape.
Keep the area still and get help.
Open breaks and breaks near the spine or head are emergencies.
goNow: Bone sticking out of the skin, or heavy bleeding
Neck, back or head injury: do not move the person: call 911
Numb, cold or blue fingers or toes below the injury
Cannot move or put weight on the limb

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A fracture is a crack or break in a bone. It usually follows a fall, accident or in weak bones, a small knock. A doctor will take an X-ray. Setting and a cast or surgery are needed so the bone heals straight.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Severe pain and swelling
Bruising
The limb looks bent or cannot move
A grinding sound or feel
Numbness

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Keep the injured part still, support it with a rolled cloth or splint
Do not try to straighten it
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth
Do not eat or drink if surgery may be needed
Go to the nearest emergency room

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Make the home safe from falls
Keep bones strong with calcium and vitamin D
Wear helmets and seat belts

topics.title: Preventing falls
short: Falls are a top cause of injury in older people.
Strength, balance and a safe home prevent most of them.
A fall with a head knock or hip pain needs a doctor.
goNow: A fall with a head injury, drowsiness, vomiting or confusion
Hip or leg pain and unable to stand
Fall with heavy bleeding or numbness

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: One in three older people falls each year. Causes include weak legs, poor balance, bad eyesight, some medicines, wet floors, loose rugs, poor lighting and low blood pressure. Most falls can be prevented by exercise and home changes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Unsteady walking
Dizziness
Fear of falling
Holding on to furniture

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Do balance and leg exercises, like standing on one foot while holding a chair
Remove loose rugs and clutter
Use night lights and non-slip mats
Wear shoes that grip
Ask your doctor to review medicines

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Strength and balance exercises
Eye checks yearly
Handrails in bathroom and stairs
Stand up slowly

videos.title: Falls: level 1 balance and strength exercises

topics.title: Sprain and strain
short: A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament, and a strain is a pulled muscle.
Remember: rest, ice, a snug wrap and raise it.
A joint you cannot use may be broken.
goNow: Cannot put weight on the limb or the joint looks out of shape
Numbness, or cold and blue toes or fingers
Severe pain or a pop at the time of injury

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A sprain happens when a ligament is stretched too far, as when you twist an ankle. A strain is a pulled or torn muscle. Both cause pain, swelling and bruising. Mild ones heal in days to weeks with simple care. If you cannot put weight on it, get an X-ray.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Pain
Swelling
Bruising
Hard to move or put weight
Sometimes a pop at the time

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rest the joint for a day or two
Apply a cold pack for 15 minutes every few hours
Wrap with an elastic bandage that is snug but not tight
Raise the limb above heart level
Paracetamol for pain

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Warm up before exercise
Wear proper shoes
Strengthen muscles
Be careful on wet or uneven ground

topics.title: Muscle cramps
short: A cramp is a sudden, tight, painful muscle squeeze.
It is common in the legs at night.
Stretching and water usually help.
goNow: Cramps with weakness or numbness
Cramps with swelling, redness or warmth in one leg
Frequent cramps without a clear cause

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Muscle cramps come from tired muscles, dehydration, low salts or some medicines. They are common at night and in older people. They usually go away by themselves in seconds or minutes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
A sudden hard knot in the muscle
Pain that lasts seconds to minutes
Soreness afterwards

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Gently stretch and massage the muscle
Walk around
Warm cloth on the tight muscle
Drink water, especially after sweating
Eat bananas and leafy greens

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink enough water
Stretch before bed
Warm up before exercise
Review medicines with a doctor

topics.title: Carpal tunnel and numb hands
short: A squeezed nerve in the wrist makes the fingers tingle or go numb.
It is worse at night or with repeated hand use.
A wrist splint and rest often help.
goNow: Weakness or loss of the grip
Numbness with weakness in the face or arm or trouble speaking
Constant numbness that does not ease

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The carpal tunnel is a narrow passage in the wrist. When the nerve inside is squeezed, you feel tingling or numbness in the thumb, index and middle fingers. It is more common in people who use their hands a lot, in pregnancy and with diabetes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Tingling or numbness in the thumb and first 3 fingers
Pain waking you at night
Dropping things
Weak grip

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Wear a wrist splint at night
Rest the hand and take breaks
Shake the hand out when numb
Keep the wrist straight while typing
See a doctor if no better in weeks

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Take breaks from repeated hand work
Keep wrists straight
Control diabetes and weight

topics.title: Lupus
short: Lupus is an illness where the body's defence attacks its own tissues.
It can affect skin, joints, kidneys and more.
Regular care and medicine keep most people well.
goNow: Chest pain or trouble breathing
Swelling of the face and legs with foamy urine
Fits, severe headache or confusion
Fever above 38.5 C with a flare

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Lupus is an autoimmune disease that causes swelling in different parts of the body. It is more common in women. Signs come and go in flares. Sunlight can trigger flares. Medicines can control it, and regular check-ups catch kidney and other problems early.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Butterfly-shaped rash on the face
Joint pain
Tiredness and fever
Mouth sores
Sun-sensitive skin

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take medicine every day
Use sunscreen, hats and shade
Rest and manage stress
Keep all follow-ups and urine tests
Do not smoke

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
It cannot be prevented
Avoid strong sun
Stay up to date with vaccines

topics.title: Widespread body pain
short: Fibromyalgia causes pain all over the body and deep tiredness.
Tests are normal, but the pain is real.
Gentle exercise and sleep help most.
goNow: Chest pain or trouble breathing
Fever, swelling or redness of a joint
Thoughts of hurting yourself: call 1553 or 911

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Fibromyalgia causes long-term pain in muscles and soft tissues, with tiredness, poor sleep and trouble thinking. The cause is unclear. Doctors first rule out other illness. Exercise, sleep care, and talking therapy often help more than medicine.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Widespread pain for months
Tiredness
Poor sleep
Foggy thinking
Tender spots

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Gentle daily exercise such as walking or swimming
Regular sleep time
Warm baths
Pace yourself
Ask your doctor about treatment

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Stay active
Sleep well
Manage stress

topics.title: Fever in a child
short: Fever is the body fighting an infection. It is a sign, not an illness by itself.
How sick the child looks matters more than the number.
Fluids and rest help. Watch for the warning signs.
goNow: A baby under 3 months with a fever of 38 C or more
Stiff neck, fits, a rash that does not fade when pressed, or very hard to wake
Fast or hard breathing, blue lips, or cannot drink
Fever for 2 days or more, or a child who looks very ill

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A fever is a body temperature of 38 C or more. It often comes with colds, flu, ear infections, dengue and other infections. Most fevers in children settle in a few days. Look at how the child acts. A child who plays and drinks is usually less worrying than one who is limp and will not drink.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Hot skin, flushed face, chills
Tired or cranky
Not wanting to eat
Sweating when the fever breaks

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Give plenty of fluids, breast milk or oral rehydration salts
Light clothes and a cool room, no cold baths
Paracetamol by the weight on the pack if the child is uncomfortable
Never give aspirin to a child
Check often and see a doctor if unsure
Do not rub with alcohol or give cold baths

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wash hands often
Keep vaccines up to date
Keep sick children home
Clean up standing water against dengue

topics.title: Dehydration
short: Dehydration means the body has lost more water than it has taken in.
It is common with diarrhoea, vomiting, fever and hot weather.
Babies, small children and older people get dry fastest.
goNow: Very sleepy, confused or hard to wake
Cannot drink, or keeps vomiting everything
No urine for 8 hours (baby: no wet diaper for 6 hours), sunken eyes, cold hands
Fast heartbeat with fainting

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: When we lose water through sweat, vomit or loose stools and do not drink enough, the body runs dry. Mild dehydration can be treated at home with fluids. Severe dehydration is an emergency, especially in babies and older people.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Thirst and dry mouth
Dark yellow urine, or very little
Dizziness
Tired and cranky
Baby: sunken soft spot, no tears when crying

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Sip small amounts often
Use oral rehydration salts (ORS) made up as the pack says
Keep feeding breast milk to babies
Rest in a cool place
Wait ten minutes after a vomit, then start sips again

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink water through the day, more in hot weather
Start ORS at the first loose stool
Do not wait to feel thirsty if you are old or working in the heat

topics.title: Newborn baby care
short: A newborn needs warmth, milk, clean hands and close skin-to-skin time.
Newborns can get sick fast, so know the warning signs.
The first check-up and vaccines are in the first week.
goNow: Fever of 38 C or more, or a body that feels cold
Hard or fast breathing, or blue lips
Will not feed, very sleepy, or yellow skin on the first day
A cord stump that is red, smelly or oozing pus, or fits

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The first month is the time of greatest need. A healthy newborn feeds every two to three hours, sleeps a lot, and wets several diapers a day. Put the baby on your chest soon after birth. Breast milk alone is best for the first six months.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Eats eight or more times a day
Wet diapers six or more times a day after day 5
Alert for short periods
Gains weight after the first week

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Wash your hands before holding the baby
Keep the cord dry and clean, do not put anything on it
Skin-to-skin contact to keep warm
Put the baby to sleep on the back, on a firm bed, with nothing loose
Newborn screening at 24 to 48 hours

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Go to prenatal check-ups
Give birth with a trained health worker
Breastfeed
Vaccines on time
Keep smokers away from the baby

topics.title: Breastfeeding
short: Breast milk alone is the best food for a baby for the first 6 months.
Start in the first hour after birth. Feed often, day and night.
Most mothers can make enough milk with support.
goNow: A baby with no wet diaper for 6 hours, or very sleepy and will not feed
Red, hot, painful breast with fever and chills
A baby who is yellow, floppy or breathing fast

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Breast milk has what a baby needs and protects against infections like diarrhoea and pneumonia. After six months, add soft foods and keep breastfeeding up to two years or more. Pain, sore nipples and low milk are common and often get better with help.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
A deep latch with the mouth wide
Swallowing sounds while feeding
The baby is calm after feeding
Six or more wet diapers a day

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Feed on demand, at least eight times a day
Skin-to-skin contact helps milk flow
Fix the latch if the nipple hurts
Drink water, eat well and rest
Ask a nurse or lactation counsellor for help

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Start early
Get breastfeeding help from the health centre
Treat sore breasts early
Ask a doctor before using formula

topics.title: Vaccines for children
short: Vaccines teach the body to fight a germ before it can make the child sick.
Free vaccines are given at the barangay health centre.
Late vaccines can still be given. Ask the nurse.
goNow: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or hives soon after a vaccine
High fever that does not go down, fits, or a child who cannot be woken

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Vaccines protect against diseases like measles, polio, TB, hepatitis B, diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus. The Philippine program gives them free in the first year, with boosters later. A sore arm or mild fever for a day or two is common and goes away.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text: Normal after a shot: a sore spot, mild fever, fussiness for a day or two

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Bring the baby's vaccine card to every visit
Give paracetamol for fever if the nurse says so
Keep the shot place clean and dry
A mild cold is not a reason to skip a visit

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Follow the schedule from birth
Adults need tetanus and flu shots too
Pregnant women need tetanus shots
Keep the card safe

topics.title: Malnutrition and stunting
short: A child who does not get enough good food may be thin, short or often sick.
The first 1,000 days of life matter most.
Healthy food, clean water and check-ups help children grow.
goNow: A child with swollen feet, very thin, very sleepy or too weak to eat
Cannot drink, or vomiting and diarrhoea with weakness

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Malnutrition can mean too little food, or food that lacks protein, iron and vitamins. Children may be underweight, too short for their age, or have thin arms. The body then fights infection poorly. It is more common where food is short, but repeated illness can cause it too.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Weight or height below the growth chart
Thin arms and legs
Tired, often sick
Slow to learn or play

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Feed eggs, fish, beans, vegetables, fruit and rice
Feed small amounts often
Keep breastfeeding as long as possible
Visit the barangay for weighing and vitamin A
Ask the health worker about special feeding for severe cases

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Breast milk alone for six months
Add family foods after six months
Give clean water
Treat worms and diarrhoea

topics.title: Healthy eating for children
short: Children need a mix of foods: rice, protein, vegetables, fruit and milk or water.
Small portions, often. Never force-feed.
Cut sugary drinks and instant snacks.
goNow: A child who cannot swallow, chokes often or has swelling of the lips after eating
Weight loss with tiredness, or cannot keep food down

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Good food helps a child grow, learn and fight germs. Fruit and vegetables, fish, eggs, beans and a little meat give protein, vitamins and iron. Sweet drinks and chips fill the stomach but give little. Many young children are picky, and that is normal.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Growing steadily on the growth chart
Active and curious
Regular stools

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Offer new foods many times
Eat together as a family
Water or milk in place of soda
Snacks of fruit, boiled egg or kamote
Small portions

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Limit sweet drinks and instant noodles
Wash fruit and vegetables
Keep up regular weighing

topics.title: Ear infection
short: Ear infections are common in small children after a cold.
Pain in the ear, pulling at the ear and fever are the usual signs.
Many get better by themselves in a few days.
goNow: Stiff neck, a swelling or redness behind the ear, or severe headache
Fever of 39 C or more, or a baby under 6 months with any fever
Pus or blood draining from the ear, or the child seems very sleepy

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Germs get into the space behind the eardrum, often after a cold. Fluid builds up and presses on the drum. Children get them more than adults because their ear tubes are short. Some need antibiotics, so a doctor should look.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Ear pain, pulling or rubbing the ear
Fever
Trouble sleeping
Cranky, less hearing
Fluid from the ear

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Paracetamol for pain by the weight on the pack
A warm cloth on the ear
Do not put anything in the ear, no oil or cotton buds
Keep the ear dry
See a doctor if it does not settle in 2 to 3 days

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Breastfeed
Keep vaccines up to date
Avoid smoke around children
Wash hands to prevent colds

topics.title: Pregnancy and prenatal care
short: Regular check-ups keep both mother and baby safe.
Go to every visit the health centre sets, at least 4; 8 is better.
Eat well, take folic acid and iron if advised, and avoid alcohol and smoking.
goNow: Bleeding from the vagina
Strong tummy pain, or the baby moves much less
Water breaks early, or labour before 37 weeks
Bad headache, blurred vision, swelling of the face or hands
Fits, fainting, high fever or trouble breathing: call 911

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Pregnancy lasts about 40 weeks. Check-ups look at blood pressure, weight, sugar and the baby's growth. Free care is available at the barangay health centre and rural health unit. A trained health worker should attend the birth.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Missed period, nausea, tiredness
Tender breasts
Passing urine often
The baby starts to move around 5 months

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Take folic acid and iron if advised
Eat more fruit, vegetables, fish and eggs
Rest and drink water
Take tetanus shots
Avoid alcohol, smoking and herbal remedies unless a doctor says so

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Go to every check-up
Plan where to give birth
Know the warning signs
Treat anemia early

topics.title: Pre-eclampsia (high blood pressure in pregnancy)
short: Pre-eclampsia is high blood pressure that starts in the second half of pregnancy.
It can harm the mother and the baby if not treated.
It is found at check-ups. That is another reason to go.
goNow: Severe headache, blurred vision or flashing lights
Pain under the ribs on the right side
Swelling of the face and hands, or sudden weight gain
Fits: call 911 now
A baby that moves much less
Trouble breathing
These signs can also start in the 6 weeks after birth

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In pre-eclampsia blood pressure rises and the kidneys leak protein. It usually starts after week 20. It can lead to fits (eclampsia) or to early birth. Treatment may include medicine and, at times, early delivery to keep both safe.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Blood pressure 140/90 or higher
Protein in the urine
Swelling of the face and hands
Bad headache or vision changes

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Go to every check-up
Rest on your left side
Follow your doctor's plan and medicine
Know when to go to hospital

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Early and regular prenatal care
Tell your doctor if you had it before, or have high blood pressure or diabetes
Ask if low-dose aspirin is right for you

topics.title: Fits with fever in a child
short: Some young children have a fit when the fever rises quickly.
It looks scary but is usually harmless and lasts under 5 minutes.
Stay calm. Keep the child safe, and always get a check.
goNow: A fit that lasts more than 5 minutes: call 911 or go to hospital now
Trouble breathing, blue lips, or the child does not wake up after
A stiff neck, vomiting, or a rash
A first fit, so see a doctor the same day

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: A febrile seizure is a fit with fever in a child aged about 6 months to 5 years. The body shakes for a minute or two, and the child may go stiff and unresponsive. It does not cause brain damage in most cases, but a doctor should find the cause of the fever.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Shaking of arms and legs
Eyes rolling up
Unresponsive for a minute or two
Sleepy after

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Lay the child on their side on a soft surface
Clear things away, do not hold them down
Do not put anything in the mouth
Note the time the fit starts
Do not give anything by mouth until the child is fully awake

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Treat infections early
Keep vaccines up to date
Paracetamol makes a child comfortable but does not stop a fit

topics.title: Yellow baby (newborn jaundice)
short: Many newborns look yellow in the first week. Most are fine.
Yellow in the first 24 hours, or deep yellow, needs a doctor.
Frequent feeds help clear it.
goNow: Yellow skin in the first 24 hours of life
Yellow that spreads to the legs or lasts more than 2 weeks
A baby who is very sleepy, will not feed, or has a high-pitched cry
Pale stools or dark urine

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: The liver is not yet working fully at birth, so a yellow substance (bilirubin) builds up. Most cases are mild. If the level goes too high it can harm the brain, so a doctor may use light treatment (phototherapy).

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Yellow skin and eyes
Sleepy and feeds poorly
Dark urine, pale stools

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Feed often, at least 8 times a day
Do not rely on sunbathing the baby, see a health worker
Go for a check by day 3 to 5
Ask the doctor about light therapy

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Give birth with a trained health worker
Check blood types in pregnancy
Go for early baby check-ups

topics.title: Baby crying and colic
short: Some healthy babies cry for hours in the first months. It is called colic.
It usually peaks at 6 weeks and stops by 4 months.
Check for fever, hunger and a wet diaper first.
goNow: Fever of 38 C or more in a baby under 3 months
Vomiting green fluid, blood in stools, or a hard swollen tummy
A baby who is limp, hard to wake, or cries weakly

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Colic means crying for more than three hours a day, three days a week, in an otherwise healthy baby. Nobody knows the cause. It is not caused by anything you did. Rule out hunger, pain, a hair wrapped around a toe, or a hot room.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Crying at the same time each day, often evening
Clenched fists, arched back
Feeds and grows well between crying

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Hold and rock the baby
Gentle tummy massage
A warm bath
Burp after feeds
If you feel at your limit, lay the baby safely in the crib and take a short break. Never shake a baby

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Burp the baby during feeds
Ask for help from family
Keep calm

topics.title: Diaper rash
short: Red sore skin under the diaper is common and easy to treat.
Keep the skin clean and dry.
Air time without a diaper helps most.
goNow: Fever with the rash
Blisters, open sores, or pus
A rash that does not get better in 3 days

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Wet or dirty diapers rub the skin and make it red and sore. Sometimes a yeast infection grows, with bright red patches and small red spots around the edge.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Red, shiny skin in the diaper area
Sore when touched
Small bumps or patches

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Change diapers often
Clean gently with water and let dry
A zinc oxide cream at each change
Let the baby go diaper-free for a while
Do not use powder

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Change soon after a wet or dirty diaper
Wash hands
Look for a better fit

topics.title: Teething and baby teeth
short: Babies get their first teeth between 4 and 7 months.
It makes them drool and chew, but it does not cause high fever.
Start cleaning teeth with the first tooth.
goNow: Fever of 38.5 C or more, or a baby who is very unwell
Diarrhoea or rash with teething

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Teething can make gums sore and swollen. It may cause drooling, chewing and cranky nights. A fever of 38 C or more, vomiting or diarrhoea is not from teething, so look for other causes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Drooling
Chewing on things
Swollen gums
Cranky

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Rub the gums with a clean finger
A cool, clean teething ring
Wipe the mouth
Brush the teeth with a rice-grain amount of fluoride toothpaste twice a day

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
No sugary drinks in a bottle at night
First dental visit by age 1
Brush twice a day

topics.title: Teeth and gum care
short: Brushing twice a day and fewer sweets keep teeth healthy.
A toothache needs a dentist, not just pain pills.
Children and older people need extra care.
goNow: Swelling of the face or under the jaw with a toothache
Fever with a swollen face, or trouble swallowing or breathing
A knocked-out tooth: see a dentist within an hour

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Cavities form when germs in the mouth turn sugar to acid and it eats the tooth. Gum disease comes from plaque left at the gum line. Both are common and mostly preventable. Poor mouth health can also affect the heart and diabetes.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Tooth pain that wakes you
Pain with hot or cold
Bleeding or red gums
Bad breath that stays
A hole or black spot

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Brush for two minutes, twice a day, with fluoride toothpaste
Clean between the teeth once a day
Rinse with warm salt water for pain
Cut sweet drinks and snacks
See a dentist at least once a year

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Brush and floss
Few sweets
Check-ups every 6 months to a year
Do not smoke

topics.title: Eczema and itchy skin
short: Eczema makes skin dry, red and itchy. It comes and goes.
It is not catching. It often begins in babies.
Moisturise every day and avoid triggers.
goNow: Skin that is weeping, crusted or has pus, with fever
Blisters or sores spreading quickly
Eczema with a swollen face or trouble breathing after a new food or medicine

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Eczema is a long-term skin problem where the skin barrier is weak. It runs in families with asthma and hay fever. Hot weather, sweat, soap, wool and stress can set it off. Scratching makes it worse.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Dry, red, itchy patches
Rough skin in elbow and knee folds
Cracks or oozing when scratched
Poor sleep from itching

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Put on a thick moisturiser right after a short lukewarm bath
Use mild soap or none
Cotton clothes
Trim fingernails short
Ask the doctor about a mild steroid cream during flares

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Moisturise daily
Avoid known triggers
Keep cool
Treat infected skin early

topics.title: Menopause
short: Menopause is when periods stop for good, usually around age 50.
Hot flashes and poor sleep are common but pass with time.
Bones and the heart need extra care after.
goNow: Heavy bleeding, or bleeding after periods have stopped for a year
Chest pain or trouble breathing
Feeling very down or having thoughts of harming yourself

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: When the ovaries make less hormone, periods stop. Menopause is confirmed after 12 months with no period. Symptoms can last several years. It is a normal change, not an illness.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Hot flashes and night sweats
Trouble sleeping
Mood changes
Dry vagina
Lighter or irregular periods before they stop

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Dress in layers and keep cool
Regular exercise
Enough calcium and vitamin D
Do not smoke
Talk to a doctor about treatment options

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Healthy diet and weight
Walk daily
Check bone health after 50
Regular check-ups

topics.title: Family planning
short: Family planning lets you space your children and protect your health.
Many methods are free at the health centre.
Condoms also protect against infections.
goNow: Severe tummy pain, or a missed period with pain after an IUD or implant
Sudden leg swelling and pain, chest pain or trouble breathing while on the pill
Heavy bleeding that soaks a pad every hour

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Methods include condoms, pills, injections, implants, IUDs, and calendar methods. A health worker can help you pick one that suits your health and wishes. The emergency pill works best soon after sex.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text: Common in the first months: spotting or irregular periods

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Talk to a nurse or doctor about your options
Take pills at the same time each day
Use condoms to also prevent infections
Keep follow-up visits

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Plan pregnancies
Get tested for infections
Go to the health centre for free methods

topics.title: Choking
short: Choking is when food or an object blocks the airway.
A person who cannot cough, speak or breathe needs help at once.
Back blows and belly thrusts can clear the airway.
goNow: The person cannot cough, speak or breathe, or turns blue: call 911 and start back blows and thrusts now
A person who goes limp or unconscious: start CPR
A baby who is choking: back blows and chest thrusts, call 911

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: When something blocks the windpipe, air cannot get in. A person who can cough strongly should keep coughing. If they cannot cough, speak or breathe, act at once. For an adult or child: give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades, then 5 belly thrusts (Heimlich) until the object comes out. For a baby: 5 back blows then 5 chest thrusts with two fingers.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Hands clutching the throat
Cannot speak, cough or breathe
High-pitched or no sound
Face turns red then blue
Panic

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Stand behind the person, lean them forward and give 5 back blows with the heel of your hand
Then 5 belly thrusts: fist above the navel, pull in and up
Alternate until the object is out or help comes
For pregnant or very large people do chest thrusts
Everyone who was choking needs a check by a doctor after
Never do belly thrusts on a baby under 1 year

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Cut food small for children and the old
Sit down to eat, no talking or laughing with food in the mouth
Keep small objects and coins from babies
Do not give nuts or hard sweets to small children

videos.title: Mayo Clinic Minute: the Heimlich maneuver

topics.title: Burns and scalds
short: Cool the burn with running water for 20 minutes.
Do not put toothpaste, oil, ice or egg on a burn.
Big or deep burns need a hospital.
goNow: A burn larger than the person's palm, or on the face, hands, feet, groin or over a joint
A burn that is white, leathery, charred or numb
A burn from fire in a closed room, chemicals or electricity, or with trouble breathing
Any burn on a baby or an older person

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Burns happen from heat, hot liquids (scalds), fire, chemicals, electricity or sun. The first minutes matter. Cool the burn quickly with cool running water, and remove rings and watches before swelling starts. Do not pop blisters.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Red, painful skin
Blisters
White or black skin with little pain in a deep burn
Swelling

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Run cool (not ice cold) tap water over the burn for 20 minutes
Take off rings, watches and loose clothes near it, but not anything stuck to the skin
Cover loosely with a clean non-stick cloth or cling film
Paracetamol for pain
Do not use ice, butter, oil, toothpaste or egg
For a baby or a large burn, keep the rest of the body warm while cooling

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Keep hot pots and kettles out of children's reach
Turn pot handles inward
Keep matches, lighters and candles away from children
Test bath water by hand before use

videos.title: First aid for a burn

topics.title: Cuts, scrapes and wounds
short: Press on a bleeding cut with a clean cloth for 10 minutes.
Then wash with clean water and cover.
Check that your tetanus shot is up to date.
goNow: Bleeding that does not stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure
Blood that spurts, or a very deep or gaping wound
A cut from an animal, a rusty nail or dirty object when tetanus shots are not up to date
Numbness, cannot move a finger, or a part is cut off

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Most cuts are small and heal by themselves. Stop the bleeding first, then clean. A cut that is deep, gapes or is on the face may need stitches within a few hours. A dirty wound can lead to infection or tetanus.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Bleeding
Pain
Swelling around the wound
A red area that spreads or pus later means infection

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Wash your hands first
Press firmly with a clean cloth for 10 minutes without lifting
Rinse the wound with clean running water, then wash gently with soap around it
Cover with a clean bandage
Change daily and watch for redness, warmth, pus or fever

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wear gloves and shoes when working
Keep knives and tools in a safe place
Keep tetanus vaccination up to date

topics.title: Heavy bleeding
short: Press firmly on the wound with a cloth, and keep pressing.
Call 911 for bleeding that does not slow down.
Lie the person down and keep them warm.
goNow: Bleeding that soaks through a cloth, spurts, or does not slow after 10 minutes of firm pressure: call 911
The person is pale, sweaty, confused or faint
Bleeding from the head, chest or tummy after an injury
Vomiting blood or passing black or bloody stools

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Heavy bleeding can cause shock when the body loses too much blood. Pressing hard on the wound is the most important step. Do not take a cloth off if blood soaks through, add more on top and keep pressing.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Blood that soaks cloth quickly
Pale and sweaty skin
Fast pulse, weakness
Thirst and confusion

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Call 911
Press hard on the wound with a thick clean cloth
Lay the person down and raise the legs if no head or neck injury
Keep them warm
Do not give food or drink
Do not remove an object stuck in the wound

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Take care with sharp tools and glass
Wear helmets and seat belts
Ask your doctor about bleeding risk if you take blood thinners

topics.title: Snake bite
short: Keep the person calm and still. Get to a hospital fast.
Do not cut, suck or tie the bite.
Remember the colour and shape of the snake, but do not try to catch it.
goNow: Any bite from a snake that could be poisonous: go to the hospital now, by vehicle
Swelling spreading up the limb, pain, bruising or bleeding
Drooping eyelids, trouble speaking, swallowing or breathing
Dizziness, faintness or vomiting

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Some Philippine snakes, such as cobras, are venomous. Even a bite from an unknown snake needs a medical check. Hospitals give antivenom and care. Do not waste time with home remedies, which can do harm.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Two puncture marks
Pain and swelling
Bruising or bleeding
Weakness, drooping eyelids, trouble breathing

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Move away from the snake
Keep the person calm and as still as possible
Keep the bitten limb still, at or below heart level
Take off rings and tight clothing
Go to the hospital by vehicle, do not walk
Do not cut, suck, burn or tie the bite
Do not use ice
Do not go to an albularyo

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Wear boots in tall grass
Shine a light at night
Do not handle snakes
Keep the yard clear of heaps and rats

topics.title: Dog and cat bites, rabies
short: Wash any bite at once with soap and running water for 15 minutes.
Go to an animal bite centre the same day, even if the animal looks healthy.
Rabies is deadly once signs start, but shots work if given in time.
goNow: Any bite or deep scratch from a dog, cat or bat: go to an animal bite centre today
Fear of water, fits, confusion or sudden strange behaviour
A bite to the head, face or neck, or a wound that bleeds a lot

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Rabies is a virus in the spit of infected animals, mostly dogs in the Philippines. It spreads through bites and scratches. Once signs show it is almost always deadly, but rabies shots right after a bite can stop it. Animal bite centres give them free or low cost.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
A bite or scratch from an animal
Pain and tingling at the wound
Fever
Later: fear of water, confusion, fits

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Wash the wound well with soap and running water for 15 minutes
Cover loosely
Go to the animal bite centre or hospital the same day
Take all the shots on schedule
If you can, watch the animal for 14 days, but do not wait for signs to get the shots
Do not put garlic, herbs or anything else on the wound. Do not go to a tandok or albularyo instead of the bite centre

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Vaccinate dogs and cats every year
Do not tease or touch stray animals
Keep dogs on a leash
Teach children to stay away from strange animals

topics.title: Heat stroke
short: Heat stroke is an emergency. The body can no longer cool itself.
Move to the shade, cool the person down, and call 911.
Older people, babies and outdoor workers are at higher risk.
goNow: Hot, red, dry or damp skin with confusion, a fit or fainting: call 911
Body temperature above 40 C
A person who cannot drink or vomits, or stops sweating

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: In very hot weather the body may fail to cool itself. Heat exhaustion comes first with heavy sweating, weakness and a fast pulse. If not cooled, it can turn into heat stroke, which can harm the brain and organs within minutes. Cool the person immediately.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Heavy sweating, weak, dizzy
Headache and nausea
Hot, red skin
Fast pulse
Confusion, fits or fainting in heat stroke

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Move to a cool, shaded place
Loosen or take off extra clothes
Cool with wet cloths, a fan, or cool water on the skin
Give small sips of water only if the person is awake and alert
Call 911 for confusion or fainting

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Drink water through the day
Avoid heavy work at noon
Wear light clothes and a hat
Never leave a child or pet in a parked car

videos.title: Heat exhaustion and heatstroke

topics.title: Drowning and near-drowning
short: A person who is drowning cannot call for help.
Pull them out safely and call 911.
Give rescue breaths and CPR if they are not breathing.
goNow: Anyone pulled from the water who is not breathing, unresponsive or blue: call 911 and start CPR
Anyone who needed help in the water, even if they seem fine now
Coughing, vomiting or trouble breathing in the hours after

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text: Drowning can happen in a few minutes, even in shallow water. Children can drown in a bucket. The danger is lack of air. Get the person out safely, without putting yourself in danger. Throw a rope, a float or a bottle instead of jumping in.

sections.heading: Signs
sections.text:
Quiet in the water, no splashing
Head back, mouth at water level
Not breathing when pulled out
Blue lips

sections.heading: What helps at home
sections.text:
Call 911
Throw something that floats
Lay the person on their back on a firm surface
If they are not breathing normally, give 5 rescue breaths, then 30 chest pushes and 2 breaths. If you cannot give breaths, push on the chest without stopping
Place on side when breathing returns, and keep them warm
Go to the hospital even if recovered

sections.heading: Prevent it
sections.text:
Never leave a child alone near water
Fence pools and cover wells and drums
Wear life jackets on boats
Learn to swim and learn CPR

topics.title: Poisoning
short: Call 911 or the UP-PGH National Poison Management and Control Center at once. Do not make the person vomit.
Keep the container to show the doctor.
A child who swallows medicines or chemicals needs a check, even if well.
